If you want to refine existing API models,\n         * extend `Http::Client::Request` instead.\n         */\n        abstract class Range extends DataFlowNode {\n          /**\n           * Gets a data flow node that contributes to the URL of the request.\n           * Depending on the framework, a request may have multiple nodes which contribute to the URL.\n           */\n          abstract DataFlowNode getAUrlPart();\n\n          /** Gets a string that identifies the framework used for this request. */\n          abstract string getFramework();\n\n          /**\n           * Holds if this request is made using a mode that disables SSL/TLS\n           * certificate validation, where `disablingNode` represents the point at\n           * which the validation was disabled, and `argumentOrigin` represents the origin\n           * of the argument that disabled the validation (which could be the same node as\n           * `disablingNode`).\n           */\n          abstract predicate disablesCertificateValidation(\n            DataFlowNode disablingNode, DataFlowNode argumentOrigin\n          );\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n</input>\n<task>\n请你分析这段代码并完成以下任务：\n1. 提取并总结该代码所涉及的 API 信息，包括：\n   - block. */\n    Node getNode(int pos) { result = getNode(this, pos) }\n\n    /** Gets a control flow node in this basic block. */\n    Node getANode() { result = this.getNode(_) }\n\n    /** Gets the first control flow node in this basic block. */\n    Node getFirstNode() { this = TBasicBlockStart(result) }\n\n    /** Gets the last control flow node in this basic block. */\n    Node getLastNode() { result = this.getNode(this.length() - 1) }\n\n    /** Gets the length of this basic block. */\n    int length() { result = strictcount(this.getANode()) }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this basic block immediately dominates basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, this basic block is the unique basic block satisfying:\n     * 1. This basic block strictly dominates `bb`\n     * 2. There exists no other basic block that is strictly dominated by this\n     *    basic block and which strictly dominates `bb`.\n     *\n     * All basic blocks, except entry basic blocks, have a unique immediate\n     * dominator.\n     */\n    predicate immediatelyDominates(BasicBlock bb) { bbIDominates(this, bb) }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this basic block strictly dominates basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, all paths reaching `bb` from the entry point basic block must\n     * go through this basic block and this basic block is different from `bb`.\n     */\n    predicate strictlyDominates(BasicBlock bb) { bbIDominates+(this, bb) }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this basic block dominates basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, all paths reaching `bb` from the entry point basic block must\n     * go through this basic block.\n     */\n    predicate dominates(BasicBlock bb) {\n      bb = this or\n      this.strictlyDominates(bb)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `df` is in the dominance frontier of this basic block. That is,\n     * this basic block dominates a predecessor of `df`, but does not dominate\n     * `df` itself. I.e., it is equivaluent to:\n     * ```\n     * this.dominates(df.getAPredecessor()) and not this.strictlyDominates(df)\n     * ```\n     */\n    predicate inDominanceFrontier(BasicBlock df) {\n      // Algorithm from Cooper et al., \"A Simple, Fast Dominance Algorithm\" (Figure 5),\n      // who in turn attribute it to Ferrante et al., \"The program dependence graph and\n      // its use in optimization\".\n      this = df.getAPredecessor() and not bbIDominates(this, df)\n      or\n      exists(BasicBlock prev | prev.inDominanceFrontier(df) |\n        bbIDominates(this, prev) and\n        not bbIDominates(this, df)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets the basic block that immediately dominates this basic block, if any.\n     *\n     * That is, the result is the unique basic block satisfying:\n     * 1. The result strictly dominates this basic block.\n     * 2. There exists no other basic block that is strictly dominated by the\n     *    result and which strictly dominates this basic block.\n     *\n     * All basic blocks, except entry basic blocks, have a unique immediate\n     * dominator.\n     */\n    BasicBlock getImmediateDominator() { bbIDominates(result, this) }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the edge with successor type `s` out of this basic block is a\n     * dominating edge for `dominated`.\n     *\n     * That is, all paths reaching `dominated` from the entry point basic\n     * block must go through the `s` edge out of this basic block.\n     *\n     * Edge dominance is similar to node dominance except it concerns edges\n     * instead of nodes: A basic block is dominated by a _basic block_ `bb` if\n     * it can only be reached through `bb` and dominated by an _edge_ `e` if it\n     * can only be reached through `e`.\n     *\n     * Note that where all basic blocks (except the entry basic block) are\n     * strictly dominated by at least one basic block, a basic block may not be\n     * dominated by any edge. If an edge dominates a basic block `bb`, then\n     * both endpoints of the edge dominates `bb`. The converse is not the case,\n     * as there may be multiple paths between the endpoints with none of them\n     * dominating.\n     */\n    predicate edgeDominates(BasicBlock dominated, SuccessorType s) {\n      // For this block to control the block `dominated` with `s` the following must be true:\n      // 1/ Execution must have passed through the test i.e. `this` must strictly dominate `dominated`.\n      // 2/ Execution must have passed through the `s` edge leaving `this`.\n      //\n      // Although \"passed through the `s` edge\" implies that `this.getASuccessor(s)` dominates `dominated`,\n      // the reverse is not true, as flow may have passed through another edge to get to `this.getASuccessor(s)`\n      // so we need to assert that `this.getASuccessor(s)` dominates `dominated` *and* that\n      // all predecessors of `this.getASuccessor(s)` are either `this` or dominated by `this.getASuccessor(s)`.\n      //\n      // For example, in the following C# snippet:\n      // ```csharp\n      // if (x)\n      //   dominated;\n      // false_successor;\n      // uncontrolled;\n      // ```\n      // `false_successor` dominates `uncontrolled`, but not all of its predecessors are `this` (`if (x)`)\n      //  or dominated by itself. Whereas in the following code:\n      // ```csharp\n      // if (x)\n      //   while (dominated)\n      //     also_controlled;\n      // false_successor;\n      // uncontrolled;\n      // ```\n      // the block `while dominated` is dominated because all of its predecessors are `this` (`if (x)`)\n      // or (in the case of `also_controlled`) dominated by itself.\n      //\n      // The additional constraint on the predecessors of the test successor implies\n      // that `this` strictly dominates `dominated` so that isn't necessary to check\n      // directly.\n      exists(BasicBlock succ |\n        succ = this.getASuccessor(s) and dominatingEdge(this, succ) and succ.dominates(dominated)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this basic block strictly post-dominates basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, all paths reaching a normal exit point basic block from basic\n     * block `bb` must go through this basic block and this basic block is\n     * different from `bb`.\n     */\n    predicate strictlyPostDominates(BasicBlock bb) { bbIPostDominates+(this, bb) }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this basic block post-dominates basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, all paths reaching a normal exit point basic block from basic\n     * block `bb` must go through this basic block.\n     */\n    predicate postDominates(BasicBlock bb) {\n      this.strictlyPostDominates(bb) or\n      this = bb\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if this basic block is in a loop in the control flow graph. */\n    predicate inLoop() { this.getASuccessor+() = this }\n\n    /** Gets a textual representation of this basic block. */\n    string toString() { result = this.getFirstNode().toString() }\n  }\n\n  class EntryBasicBlock extends BasicBlock {\n    EntryBasicBlock() { nodeIsDominanceEntry(this.getFirstNode()) }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if `bb1` has `bb2` as a direct successor and the edge between `bb1`\n   * and `bb2` is a dominating edge.\n   *\n   * An edge `(bb1, bb2)` is dominating if there exists a basic block that can\n   * only be reached from the entry block by going through `(bb1, bb2)`. This\n   * implies that `(bb1, bb2)` dominates its endpoint `bb2`. I.e., `bb2` can\n   * only be reached from the entry block by going via `(bb1, bb2)`.\n   *\n   * This is a necessary and sufficient condition for an edge to dominate some\n   * block, and therefore `dominatingEdge(bb1, bb2) and bb2.dominates(bb3)`\n   * means that the edge `(bb1, bb2)` dominates `bb3`.\n   */\n  pragma[nomagic]\n  predicate dominatingEdge(BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2) {\n    bb1.getASuccessor(_) = bb2 and\n    bbIDominates(bb1, bb2) and\n    // The above is not sufficient to ensure that `bb2` can only be reached\n    // through `(bb1, bb2)`. To see why, consider this example corresponding to\n    // an `if` statement without an `else` block where `A` is the basic block\n    // following the `if` statement:\n    // ```\n    // ... --> cond --[true]--> ... --> A\n    //           \\                      ^\n    //            ----[false]-----------\n    // ```\n    // Here `A` is a direct successor of `cond` along the `false` edge and it\n    // is immediately dominated by `cond`, but `A` is not dominated by the\n    // `false` edge since it is also possible to reach `A` via the `true`\n    // edge.\n    //\n    // Note that the first and third conjunct implies the second. But\n    // explicitly including the second conjunct leads to a better join order.\n    forall(BasicBlock pred | pred = bb2.getAPredecessor() and pred != bb1 | bb2.dominates(pred))\n  }\n\n  cached\n  private module Cached {\n    private Node nodeGetAPredecessor(Node node, SuccessorType s) {\n      nodeGetASuccessor(result, s) = node\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if this node has more than one predecessor. */\n    private predicate nodeIsJoin(Node node) { strictcount(nodeGetAPredecessor(node, _)) > 1 }\n\n    /** Holds if this node has more than one successor. */\n    private predicate nodeIsBranch(Node node) { strictcount(nodeGetASuccessor(node, _)) > 1 }\n\n    /**\n     * Internal representation of basic blocks. (CFGs) from\n * abstract syntax trees (ASTs).\n *\n * The implementation is centered around the concept of a _completion_, which\n * models how the execution of a statement or expression terminates.\n *\n * The CFG is built by structural recursion over the AST, using the abstract class\n * `ControlFlowTree`. To achieve this, the CFG edges related to a given AST node,\n * `n`, are divided into three categories:\n *\n *   1. The in-going edge that points to the first CFG node to execute when\n *      `n` is going to be executed.\n *   2. The out-going edges for control flow leaving `n` that are going to some\n *      other node in the surrounding context of `n`.\n *   3. The edges that have both of their end-points entirely within the AST\n *      node and its children.\n *\n * The edges in (1) and (2) are inherently non-local and are therefore\n * initially calculated as half-edges, that is, the single node, `k`, of the\n * edge contained within `n`, by the predicates `k = n.first()` and `k = n.last(_)`,\n * respectively. The edges in (3) can then be enumerated directly by the predicate\n * `succ` by calling `first` and `last` recursively on the children of `n` and\n * connecting the end-points. This yields the entire CFG, since all edges are in\n * (3) for _some_ AST node.\n *\n * The parameter of `last` is the completion, which is necessary to distinguish\n * the out-going edges from `n`. Note that the completion changes as the calculation of\n * `last` proceeds outward through the AST; for example, a completion representing a\n * loop break will be caught up by its surrounding loop and turned into a normal\n * completion.\n */\nmodule MakeWithSplitting<\n  LocationSig Location, //\n  InputSig<Location> Input, //\n  SplittingInputSig<Location, Input> SplittingInput, //\n  ConditionalCompletionSplittingInputSig<Location, Input, SplittingInput> ConditionalCompletionSplittingInput>\n{\n  private import Input\n  private import SplittingInput\n\n  final private class this element. */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    abstract predicate first(AstNode first);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `last` with completion `c` is a potential last element executed\n     * within this element.\n     */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    abstract predicate last(AstNode last, Completion c);\n\n    /** Holds if abnormal execution of `child` should propagate upwards. */\n    abstract predicate abstract predicate succ(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if `first` is the first element executed within control flow\n   * element `cft`.\n   */\n  predicate The actual evaluation order is determined by the predicate\n   * `getChildNode()`.\n   */\n  abstract class StandardTree extends ControlFlowTree {\n    /** Gets the `i`th child element, in order of evaluation. */\n    abstract AstNode getChildNode(int i);\n\n    private ControlFlowTree getChildTreeRanked(int i) {\n      result =\n        rank[i + 1](ControlFlowTree child, int j | child = this.getChildNode(j) | child order by j)\n    }\n\n    /** Gets the first child node of this element. */\n    deprecated final AstNode getFirstChildNode() { result = this.getChildTreeRanked(0) }\n\n    /** Gets the first child node of this element. */\n    final ControlFlowTree getFirstChildTree() { result = this.getChildTreeRanked(0) }\n\n    /** Gets the last child node of this node. */\n    deprecated final AstNode getLastChildElement() {\n      exists(int last |\n        result = this.getChildTreeRanked(last) and\n        not exists(this.getChildTreeRanked(last + 1))\n      )\n    }\n\n    /** Gets the last child node of this node. */\n    final ControlFlowTree getLastChildTree() {\n      exists(int last |\n        result = this.getChildTreeRanked(last) and\n        not exists(this.getChildTreeRanked(last + 1))\n      )\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if this element has no children. */\n    predicate isLeafElement() { not exists(this.getFirstChildTree()) }\n\n    override predicate propagatesAbnormal(AstNode child) { child = this.getChildNode(_) }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    override predicate succ(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      exists(int i |\n        last(this.getChildTreeRanked(i), pred, c) and\n        completionIsNormal(c) and\n        first(this.getChildTreeRanked(i + 1), succ)\n      )\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** A standard element that is executed in pre-order. */\n  abstract class StandardPreOrderTree extends StandardTree, PreOrderTree {\n    override predicate last(AstNode last, Completion c) {\n      last(this.getLastChildTree(), last, c)\n      or\n      this.isLeafElement() and\n      completionIsValidFor(c, this) and\n      last = this\n    }\n\n    override predicate succ(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      StandardTree.super.succ(pred, succ, c)\n      or\n      pred = this and\n      first(this.getFirstChildTree(), succ) and\n      completionIsSimple(c)\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** A standard element that is     or\n      not exists(this.getFirstChildTree()) and\n      first = this\n    }\n\n    override predicate succ(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      StandardTree.super.succ(pred, succ, abstract class LeafTree extends PreOrderTree, PostOrderTree {\n    override predicate propagatesAbnormal(AstNode child) { none() }\n\n    override predicate succ(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c) { none() }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if split kinds `sk1` and `sk2` may overlap. That is, they may apply\n   * to at least one common AST node inside `scope`.\n   */\n  private predicate overlapping(CfgScope scope, SplitKind sk1, SplitKind sk2) {\n    exists(AstNode e |\n      sk1.appliesTo(e) and\n      sk2.appliesTo(e) and\n      scope = getCfgScope(e)\n    )\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * A split kind. Each control flow node can have at most one split of a\n   * given kind.\n   */\n  abstract class SplitKind instanceof SplitKindBase {\n    /** Gets a split of this kind. */\n    SplitImpl getASplit() { result.getKind() = this }\n\n    /** Holds if some split of this kind applies to AST node `n`. */\n    predicate appliesTo(AstNode n) { this.getASplit().appliesTo(n) }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets a unique integer representing this split kind. The integer is used\n     * to represent sets of splits as ordered lists.\n     */\n    abstract int getListOrder();\n\n    /** Gets the rank of this split kind among all overlapping kinds for `c`. */\n    private int getRank(CfgScope scope) {\n      this =\n        rank[result](SplitKind sk | overlapping(scope, this, sk) | sk order by sk.getListOrder())\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split kind is enabled for AST node `n`. For performance reasons,\n     * the number of splits is restricted by the `maxSplits()` predicate.\n     */\n    predicate isEnabled(AstNode n) {\n      this.appliesTo(n) and\n      this.getRank(getCfgScope(n)) <= maxSplits()\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets the rank of this split kind among all the split kinds that apply to\n     * AST node `n`. The rank is based on the order defined by `getListOrder()`.\n     */\n    int getListRank(AstNode n) {\n      this.isEnabled(n) and\n      this = rank[result](SplitKind sk | sk.appliesTo(n) | sk order by sk.getListOrder())\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a textual representation of this split kind. */\n    abstract string toString();\n  }\n\n  final private class SplitFinal = Split;\n\n  /** An interface for implementing an entity to split on. */\n  abstract class SplitImpl extends SplitFinal {\n    /** Gets the kind of this split. */\n    abstract SplitKind getKind();\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split is entered when control passes from `pred` to `succ` with\n     * completion `c`.\n     *\n     * Invariant: `hasEntry(pred, succ, c) implies succ(pred, succ, c)`.\n     */\n    abstract predicate hasEntry(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split is entered when control passes from `scope` to the entry point\n     * `first`.\n     *\n     * Invariant: `hasEntryScope(scope, first) implies scopeFirst(scope, first)`.\n     */\n    abstract predicate hasEntryScope(CfgScope scope, AstNode first);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split is left when control passes from `pred` to `succ` with\n     * completion `c`.\n     *\n     * Invariant: `hasExit(pred, succ, c) implies succ(pred, succ, c)`.\n     */\n    abstract predicate hasExit(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split is left when control passes from `last` out of the enclosing\n     * scope `scope` with completion `c`.\n     *\n     * Invariant: `hasExitScope(scope, last, c) implies scopeLast(scope, last, c)`\n     */\n    abstract predicate hasExitScope(CfgScope scope, AstNode last, Completion c);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this split is maintained when control passes from `pred` to `succ` with\n     * completion `c`.\n     *\n     * Invariant: `hasSuccessor(pred, succ, c) implies succ(pred, succ, c)`\n     */\n    abstract predicate hasSuccessor(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c);\n\n    /** Holds if this split applies to AST node `n`. */\n    final predicate appliesTo(AstNode n) {\n      this.hasEntry(_, n, _)\n      or\n      this.hasEntryScope(_, n)\n      or\n      exists(AstNode pred | this.appliesTo(pred) | this.hasSuccessor(pred, n, _))\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `succ` is a control flow successor for `pred`, given that `pred`\n     * finishes with completion `c`, and this split applies to `pred`.\n     */\n    pragma[noinline]\n    final predicate appliesSucc(AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      this.appliesTo(pred) and\n      succ(pred, succ, c)\n    }\n  }\n\n  private predicate isFullyConstructedSplits(Splits splits) { exists(TAstNode(_, _, splits)) }\n\n  /**\n   * A set of control flow node splits. The set is represented by a list of splits,\n   * ordered by ascending rank.\n   */\n  class Splits extends TSplits {\n    /** Gets a textual representation of this set of splits. */\n    string toString() {\n      result = splitsToString(this)\n      or\n      not isFullyConstructedSplits(this) and\n      result = \"<partial split set>\"\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a split belonging to this set of splits. */\n    SplitImpl getASplit() {\n      exists(SplitImpl head, Splits tail | this = TSplitsCons(head, tail) |\n        result = head\n        or\n        result = tail.getASplit()\n      )\n    }\n  }\n\n  private predicate succEntrySplitsFromRank(CfgScope pred, AstNode succ, Splits splits, int rnk) {\n    splits = TSplitsNil() and\n    scopeFirst(pred, succ) and\n    rnk = 0\n    or\n    exists(SplitImpl head, Splits tail | succEntrySplitsCons(pred, succ, head, tail, rnk) |\n      splits = TSplitsCons(head, tail)\n    )\n  }\n\n  private predicate succEntrySplitsCons(\n    CfgScope pred, AstNode succ, SplitImpl head, Splits tail, int rnk\n  ) {\n    succEntrySplitsFromRank(pred, succ, tail, rnk - 1) and\n    head.hasEntryScope(pred, succ) and\n    rnk = head.getKind().getListRank(succ)\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if `succ` with splits `succSplits` is the first element that is executed\n   * when entering callable `pred`.\n   */\n  pragma[noinline]\n  private predicate succEntrySplits(CfgScope pred, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, SuccessorType t) {\n    exists(int rnk |\n      scopeFirst(pred, succ) and\n      t instanceof DirectSuccessor and\n      succEntrySplitsFromRank(pred, succ, succSplits, rnk)\n    |\n      rnk = 0 and\n      not any(SplitImpl split).hasEntryScope(pred, succ)\n      or\n      rnk =\n        max(SplitImpl split | split.hasEntryScope(pred, succ) | split.getKind().getListRank(succ))\n    )\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if `pred` with splits `predSplits` can exit the enclosing callable\n   * `succ` with type `t`.\n   */\n  private predicate succExitSplits(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, CfgScope succ, SuccessorType t) {\n    exists(Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b, Completion c | pred = b.getAnElement() |\n      b.isReachable(succ, predSplits) and\n      t = getAMatchingSuccessorType(c) and\n      scopeLast(succ, pred, c) and\n      forall(SplitImpl predSplit | predSplit = predSplits.getASplit() |\n        predSplit.hasExitScope(succ, pred, c)\n      )\n    )\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Provides a predicate for the successor relation with split information,\n   * as well as logic used to construct the type `TSplits` representing sets\n   * of splits. Only sets of splits that can be reached are constructed, hence\n   * the predicates are mutually recursive.\n   *\n   * For the successor relation\n   *\n   * ```ql\n   * succSplits(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, Completion c)\n   * ```\n   *\n   * the following invariants are maintained:\n   *\n   * 1. `pred` is reachable with split set `predSplits`.\n   * 2. For all `split` in `predSplits`:\n   *    - If `split.hasSuccessor(pred, succ, c)` then `split` in `succSplits`.\n   * 3. For all `split` in `predSplits`:\n   *    - If `split.hasExit(pred, succ, c)` and not `split.hasEntry(pred, succ, c)` then\n   *      `split` not in `succSplits`.\n   * 4. For all `split` with kind not in `predSplits`:\n   *    - If `split.hasEntry(pred, succ, c)` then `split` in `succSplits`.\n   * 5. For all `split` in `succSplits`:\n   *    - `split.hasSuccessor(pred, succ, c)` and `split` in `predSplits`, or\n   *    - `split.hasEntry(pred, succ, c)`.\n   *\n   * The algorithm divides into four cases:\n   *\n   * 1. The set of splits for the successor is the same as the set of splits\n   *    for the predecessor:\n   *    a) The successor is in the same `SameSplitsBlock` as the predecessor.\n   *    b) The successor is *not* in the same `SameSplitsBlock` as the predecessor.\n   * 2. The set of splits for the successor is different from the set of splits\n   *    for the predecessor:\n   *    a) The set of splits for the successor is *maybe* non-empty.\n   *    b) The set of splits for the successor is *always* empty.\n   *\n   * Only case 2a may introduce new sets of splits, so only predicates from\n   * this case are used in the definition of `TSplits`.\n   *\n   * The predicates in this module are named after the cases above.\n   */\n  private module SuccSplits {\n    private predicate succInvariant1(\n      Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b, AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c\n    ) {\n      pred = b.getAnElement() and\n      b.isReachable(_, predSplits) and\n      succ(pred, succ, c)\n    }\n\n    private predicate case1b0(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      exists(Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b |\n        // Invariant 1\n        succInvariant1(b, pred, predSplits, succ, c)\n      |\n        (succ = b.getAnElement() implies succ = b) and\n        // Invariant 4\n        not exists(SplitImpl split | split.hasEntry(pred, succ, c))\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Case 1b.\n     *\n     * Invariants 1 and 4 hold in the base case, and invariants 2, 3, and 5 are\n     * maintained for all splits in `predSplits` (= `succSplits`), except\n     * possibly for the splits in `except`.\n     *\n     * The predicate is written using explicit recursion, as opposed to a `forall`,\n     * to avoid negative recursion.\n     */\n    private predicate case1bForall(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, Splits except\n    ) {\n      case1b0(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      except = predSplits\n      or\n      exists(SplitImpl split |\n        case1bForallCons(pred, predSplits, succ, c, split, except) and\n        split.hasSuccessor(pred, succ, c)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private predicate case1bForallCons(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitImpl exceptHead,\n      Splits exceptTail\n    ) {\n      case1bForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, TSplitsCons(exceptHead, exceptTail))\n    }\n\n    private predicate case1(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      // Case 1a\n      exists(Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b | succInvariant1(b, pred, predSplits, succ, c) |\n        succ = b.getAnElement() and\n        not succ = b\n      )\n      or\n      // Case 1b\n      case1bForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, TSplitsNil())\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private SplitImpl succInvariant1GetASplit(\n      Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b, AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c\n    ) {\n      succInvariant1(b, pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      result = predSplits.getASplit()\n    }\n\n    private predicate case2aux(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c) {\n      exists(Reachability::SameSplitsBlock b |\n        succInvariant1(b, pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n        (succ = b.getAnElement() implies succ = b)\n      |\n        succInvariant1GetASplit(b, pred, predSplits, succ, c).hasExit(pred, succ, c)\n        or\n        any(SplitImpl split).hasEntry(pred, succ, c)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `succSplits` should not inherit a split of kind `sk` from\n     * `predSplits`, except possibly because of a split in `except`.\n     *\n     * The predicate is written using explicit recursion, as opposed to a `forall`,\n     * to avoid negative recursion.\n     */\n    private predicate case2aNoneInheritedOfKindForall(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitKind sk, Splits except\n    ) {\n      case2aux(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      sk.appliesTo(succ) and\n      except = predSplits\n      or\n      exists(Splits mid, SplitImpl split |\n        case2aNoneInheritedOfKindForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, sk, mid) and\n        mid = TSplitsCons(split, except)\n      |\n        split.getKind() = any(SplitKind sk0 | sk0 != sk and sk0.appliesTo(succ))\n        or\n        split.hasExit(pred, succ, c)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate entryOfKind(\n      AstNode pred, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitImpl split, SplitKind sk\n    ) {\n      split.hasEntry(pred, succ, c) and\n      sk = split.getKind()\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if `succSplits` should not have a split of kind `sk`. */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate case2aNoneOfKind(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitKind sk\n    ) {\n      // None inherited from predecessor\n      case2aNoneInheritedOfKindForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, sk, TSplitsNil()) and\n      // None newly entered into\n      not entryOfKind(pred, succ, c, _, sk)\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if `succSplits` should not have a split of kind `sk` at rank `rnk`. */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate case2aNoneAtRank(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, int rnk\n    ) {\n      exists(SplitKind sk | case2aNoneOfKind(pred, predSplits, succ, c, sk) |\n        rnk = sk.getListRank(succ)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private SplitImpl case2auxGetAPredecessorSplit(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c\n    ) {\n      case2aux(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      result = predSplits.getASplit()\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a split that should be in `succSplits`. */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private SplitImpl case2aSome(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitKind sk\n    ) {\n      (\n        // Inherited from predecessor\n        result = case2auxGetAPredecessorSplit(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n        result.hasSuccessor(pred, succ, c)\n        or\n        // Newly entered into\n        exists(SplitKind sk0 |\n          case2aNoneInheritedOfKindForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, sk0, TSplitsNil())\n        |\n          entryOfKind(pred, succ, c, result, sk0)\n        )\n      ) and\n      sk = result.getKind()\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a split that should be in `succSplits` at rank `rnk`. */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    SplitImpl case2aSomeAtRank(AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, int rnk) {\n      exists(SplitKind sk | result = case2aSome(pred, predSplits, succ, c, sk) |\n        rnk = sk.getListRank(succ)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Case 2a.\n     *\n     * As opposed to the other cases, in this case we need to construct a new set\n     * of splits `succSplits`. Since this involves constructing the very IPA type,\n     * we cannot recurse directly over the structure of `succSplits`. Instead, we\n     * recurse over the ranks of all splits that *might* be in `succSplits`.\n     *\n     * - Invariant 1 holds in the base case,\n     * - invariant 2 holds for all splits with rank at least `rnk`,\n     * - invariant 3 holds for all splits in `predSplits`,\n     * - invariant 4 holds for all splits in `succSplits` with rank at least `rnk`,\n     *   and\n     * - invariant 4 holds for all splits in `succSplits` with rank at least `rnk`.\n     */\n    predicate case2aFromRank(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, Completion c, int rnk\n    ) {\n      case2aux(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      succSplits = TSplitsNil() and\n      rnk = max(any(SplitKind sk).getListRank(succ)) + 1\n      or\n      case2aFromRank(pred, predSplits, succ, succSplits, c, rnk + 1) and\n      case2aNoneAtRank(pred, predSplits, succ, c, rnk)\n      or\n      exists(Splits mid, SplitImpl split | split = case2aCons(pred, predSplits, succ, mid, c, rnk) |\n        succSplits = TSplitsCons(split, mid)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private SplitImpl case2aCons(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, Completion c, int rnk\n    ) {\n      case2aFromRank(pred, predSplits, succ, succSplits, c, rnk + 1) and\n      result = case2aSomeAtRank(pred, predSplits, succ, c, rnk)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Case 2b.\n     *\n     * Invariants 1, 4, and 5 hold in the base case, and invariants 2 and 3 are\n     * maintained for all splits in `predSplits`, except possibly for the splits\n     * in `except`.\n     *\n     * The predicate is written using explicit recursion, as opposed to a `forall`,\n     * to avoid negative recursion.\n     */\n    private predicate case2bForall(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, Splits except\n    ) {\n      // Invariant 1\n      case2aux(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      // Invariants 4 and 5\n      not any(SplitKind sk).appliesTo(succ) and\n      except = predSplits\n      or\n      exists(SplitImpl split | case2bForallCons(pred, predSplits, succ, c, split, except) |\n        // Invariants 2 and 3\n        split.hasExit(pred, succ, c)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private predicate case2bForallCons(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Completion c, SplitImpl exceptHead,\n      Splits exceptTail\n    ) {\n      case2bForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, TSplitsCons(exceptHead, exceptTail))\n    }\n\n    private predicate case2(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, Completion c\n    ) {\n      case2aFromRank(pred, predSplits, succ, succSplits, c, 1)\n      or\n      case2bForall(pred, predSplits, succ, c, TSplitsNil()) and\n      succSplits = TSplitsNil()\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `succ` with splits `succSplits` is a successor of type `t` for `pred`\n     * with splits `predSplits`.\n     */\n    predicate succSplits(\n      AstNode pred, Splits predSplits, AstNode succ, Splits succSplits, Completion c\n    ) {\n      case1(pred, predSplits, succ, c) and\n      succSplits = predSplits\n      or\n      case2(pred, predSplits, succ, succSplits, c)\n    }\n  }\n\n  private import SuccSplits\n\n  /** Provides logic for calculating reachable control flow nodes. */\n  private module Reachability {\n    /**\n     * Holds if `n` is an AST node where the set of possible splits may\n     * be different from the set of possible splits for one of `n`'s predecessors.\n     * That is, `n` starts a new block of elements with the same set of splits.\n     */\n    private predicate startsSplits(AstNode n) {\n      scopeFirst(_, n)\n      or\n      exists(SplitImpl s |\n        s.hasEntry(_, n, _)\n        or\n        s.hasExit(_, n, _)\n      )\n      or\n      exists(AstNode pred, SplitImpl split, Completion c | succ(pred, n, c) |\n        split.appliesTo(pred) and\n        not split.hasSuccessor(pred, n, c)\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate intraSplitsSucc(AstNode pred, AstNode succ) {\n      succ(pred, succ, _) and\n      not startsSplits(succ)\n    }\n\n    private predicate splitsBlockContains(AstNode start, AstNode n) =\n      fastTC(intraSplitsSucc/2)(start, n)\n\n    /**\n     * A block of control flow elements where the set of splits is guaranteed\n     * to remain unchanged, represented by the first element in the block.\n     */\n    class SameSplitsBlock extends AstNodeFinal {\n      SameSplitsBlock() { startsSplits(this) }\n\n      /** Gets a control flow element in this block. */\n      AstNode getAnElement() {\n        splitsBlockContains(this, result)\n        or\n        result = this\n      }\n\n      pragma[noinline]\n      private SameSplitsBlock getASuccessor(Splits predSplits, Splits succSplits) {\n        exists(AstNode pred | pred = this.getAnElement() |\n          succSplits(pred, predSplits, result, succSplits, _)\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if the elements of this block are reachable from a callable entry\n       *  point, with the splits `splits`.\n       */\n      predicate isReachable(CfgScope scope, Splits splits) {\n        // Base case\n        succEntrySplits(scope, this, splits, _)\n        or\n        // Recursive case\n        exists(SameSplitsBlock pred, Splits predSplits | pred.isReachable(scope, predSplits) |\n          this = pred.getASuccessor(predSplits, splits)\n        )\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  cached\n  private module Cached {\n    cached\n    newtype TSplits predSplits, succ, tail, c, rnk + 1) and\n          head = case2aSomeAtRank(pred, predSplits, succ, c, rnk)\n        )\n        or\n        succEntrySplitsCons(_, _, head, tail, _)\n      }\n\n    private string getSplitStringAt(Splits split, int index) {\n      exists(SplitImpl head, Splits tail | split = TSplitsCons(head, tail) |\n        index = 0 and result = head.toString() and result != isFullyConstructedSplits(splits) and\n      result = getSplitStringAt(splits, index)\n    }\n\n    cached\n    string splitsToString(Splits splits) {\n      result =\n        concat(string child, int succExitSplits(b.getAnElement(), _, scope, t) and\n          if isAbnormalExitType(t) then normal = false else normal = true\n        )\n      } or\n      TExitNode(CfgScope scope) {\n result = TAstNode(scope, succElement, succSplits) and\n        pred = TEntryNode(scope) and\n        succEntrySplits(scope, succElement, succSplits, t)\n      )\n      or\n      exists(CfgScope scope, exists(boolean normal |\n          result = TAnnotatedExitNode(pragma[only_bind_into](scope), normal) and\n          succExitSplits(predElement, predSplits, scope, t) and\n          if abrupt) { result = TCons(abrupt, this) }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets the stack resulting from popping a value, if any, consistent with\n     * leaving a finally block through a specific edge.\n     *\n     * The `abrupt` value indicates whether the edge has an `AbruptSuccessor`\n     * or not.\n     */\n    FinallyStack leave(Boolean abrupt) {\n      this = TNil() and result = TNil() and exists(abrupt)\n      or\n      abrupt = false and this = TCons(false, result)\n      or\n      abrupt = true and this = TCons(_, result)\n    }\n  }\n\n  private ControlFlowNode basicBlockEndPoint() {\n    result = any(BasicBlock bb).getNode(0) or\n    result = any(BasicBlock bb).getLastNode()\n  }\n\n  private predicate inFinally(AstNode node, FinallyBlock finally) {\n    node = getEnclosingAstNode(basicBlockEndPoint()) and\n    hasEnclosingFinally(node, finally)\n    or\n    exists(FinallyBlock inner | nestedFinally(inner, finally) and inFinally(node, inner))\n  }\n\n  private predicate irrelevantFinally(FinallyBlock finally) {\n    exists(BasicBlock bb, AstNode n1, AstNode n2 |\n      n1 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb.getNode(0)) and\n      n2 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb.getLastNode())\n    |\n      inFinally(n1, finally) and not inFinally(n2, finally)\n      or\n      not inFinally(n1, finally) and inFinally(n2, finally)\n    )\n  }\n\n  private predicate entersFinally(\n    BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, boolean abrupt, FinallyBlock finally\n  ) {\n    exists(AstNode n1, AstNode n2, SuccessorType t |\n      not irrelevantFinally(finally) and\n      bb1.getASuccessor(t) = bb2 and\n      n1 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb1.getLastNode()) and\n      n2 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb2.getNode(0)) and\n      not inFinally(n1, finally) and\n      inFinally(n2, finally) and\n      if t instanceof AbruptSuccessor then abrupt = true else abrupt = false\n    )\n  }\n\n  private predicate leavesFinally(\n    BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, boolean abrupt, FinallyBlock finally\n  ) {\n    exists(AstNode n1, AstNode n2, SuccessorType t |\n      not irrelevantFinally(finally) and\n      bb1.getASuccessor(t) = bb2 and\n      n1 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb1.getLastNode()) and\n      n2 = getEnclosingAstNode(bb2.getNode(0)) and\n      inFinally(n1, finally) and\n      not inFinally(n2, finally) and\n      if t instanceof AbruptSuccessor then abrupt = true else abrupt = false\n    )\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if the value of `def` is `gv`.\n   *\n   * If multiple values apply, including a singleton, then we only include the\n   * singleton.\n   */\n  private predicate ssaHasValue(SsaExplicitWrite def, GuardValue gv) {\n    exists(Expr e |\n      def.getValue() = e and\n      exprHasValue(e, gv) and\n      (any(GuardValue gv0 | exprHasValue(e, gv0)).isSingleton() implies gv.isSingleton())\n    )\n  }\n\n  pragma[nomagic]\n  private predicate ssaLiveAtEndOfBlock(SourceVariable var, SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb) {\n    def.getSourceVariable() = var and\n    def.isLiveAtEndOfBlock(bb)\n  }\n\n  pragma[nomagic]\n  private predicate initSsaValue0(\n    SourceVariable var, BasicBlock bb, SsaDefinition t, GuardValue val, boolean isSingleton\n  ) {\n    ssaLiveAtEndOfBlock(var, t, bb) and\n    (\n      ssaControls(t, bb, val)\n      or\n      ssaHasValue(t, val)\n    ) and\n    if val.isSingleton() then isSingleton = true else isSingleton = false\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if the value of `t` in `bb` is `val` and that `t` is live at the\n   * end of `bb`.\n   *\n   * If multiple values apply, including a singleton, then we only include the\n   * singleton.\n   *\n   * The underlying variable of `t` is `var`.\n   */\n  private predicate initSsaValue(SourceVariable var, BasicBlock bb, SsaDefinition t, GuardValue val) {\n    exists(boolean isSingleton |\n      initSsaValue0(var, bb, t, val, isSingleton) and\n      (initSsaValue0(var, bb, t, _, true) implies isSingleton = true)\n    )\n  }\n\n  private module GuardValueOption = Option<GuardValue>;\n\n  private class GuardValueOption = GuardValueOption::Option;\n\n  /**\n   * Gets the best constraint of `v1` and `v2`. If both are non-singletons,\n   * then we arbitrarily choose `v1`. This operation approximates intersection.\n   */\n  bindingset[v1, v2]\n  pragma[inline_late]\n  private GuardValueOption intersect(GuardValueOption v1, GuardValue v2) {\n    if v2.isSingleton()\n    then result.asSome() = v2\n    else\n      if v1.isNone()\n      then result.asSome() = v2\n      else result = v1\n  }\n\n  /** An input configuration for control flow reachability. */\n  signature module ConfigSig {\n    /**\n     * Holds if the value of `def` at `node` is a source for the reachability\n     * computation.\n     */\n    predicate source(ControlFlowNode node, SsaDefinition def);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the value of `def` at `node` is a sink for the reachability\n     * computation.\n     */\n    predicate sink(ControlFlowNode node, SsaDefinition def);\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the value of `gv` is a barrier for the reachability computation.\n     * That is, paths where the tracked variable can be inferred to have the\n     * value of `gv` are excluded from the reachability analysis.\n     */\n    default predicate barrierValue(GuardValue gv) { none() }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the edge from `bb1` to `bb2` should be excluded from the\n     * reachability analysis.\n     */\n    default predicate barrierEdge(BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2) { none() }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if flow through uncertain SSA updates should be included.\n     */\n    default predicate uncertainFlow() { any() }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Constructs a control flow reachability computation.\n   */\n  module Flow<ConfigSig Config> {\n    private predicate ssaRelevantAtEndOfBlock(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb) {\n      def.isLiveAtEndOfBlock(bb)\n      or\n      def.getBasicBlock().strictlyPostDominates(bb)\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate isSource(\n      ControlFlowNode src, SsaDefinition srcDef, SourceVariable var, BasicBlock bb, int i\n    ) {\n      Config::source(src, srcDef) and\n      bb.getNode(i) = src and\n      srcDef.getSourceVariable() = var\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate isSink(\n      ControlFlowNode sink, SsaDefinition sinkDef, SourceVariable var, BasicBlock bb, int i\n    ) {\n      Config::sink(sink, sinkDef) and\n      bb.getNode(i) = sink and\n      sinkDef.getSourceVariable() = var\n    }\n\n    private predicate uncertainStep(SsaDefinition def1, SsaDefinition def2) {\n      def2.(SsaUncertainWrite).getPriorDefinition() = def1 and\n      Config::uncertainFlow()\n    }\n\n    private predicate intraBlockStep(SsaDefinition def1, SsaDefinition def2) {\n      exists(BasicBlock bb |\n        uncertainStep(def1, def2) and\n        bb = def2.getBasicBlock() and\n        isSource(_, _, _, bb, _) and\n        isSink(_, _, _, bb, _)\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate intraBlockFlowAll(\n      ControlFlowNode src, SsaDefinition srcDef, int i, ControlFlowNode sink, SsaDefinition sinkDef,\n      int j\n    ) {\n      exists(SourceVariable var, BasicBlock bb |\n        isSource(src, srcDef, var, bb, i) and\n        isSink(sink, sinkDef, var, bb, j) and\n        i <= j and\n        intraBlockStep*(srcDef, sinkDef)\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate intraBlockFlow(\n      ControlFlowNode src, SsaDefinition srcDef, ControlFlowNode sink, SsaDefinition sinkDef\n    ) {\n      exists(int i, int j |\n        intraBlockFlowAll(src, srcDef, i, sink, sinkDef, j) and\n        not exists(int k |\n          intraBlockFlowAll(src, srcDef, i, _, _, k) and\n          k < j\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate sourceBlock(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb, ControlFlowNode src) {\n      isSource(src, def, _, bb, _) and\n      not intraBlockFlow(src, def, _, _)\n    }\n\n    private predicate sinkBlock(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb, ControlFlowNode sink) {\n      sink =\n        min(ControlFlowNode n, int i | bb.getNode(i) = n and Config::sink(n, def) | n order by i)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the edge from `bb1` to `bb2` implies that `def` has a value\n     * that is considered a barrier.\n     */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate ssaValueBarrierEdge(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2) {\n      exists(GuardValue v |\n        ssaControlsBranchEdge(def, bb1, bb2, v) and\n        Config::barrierValue(v)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate phiBlock(BasicBlock bb, SourceVariable v) {\n      exists(SsaPhiDefinition phi | phi.getBasicBlock() = bb and phi.getSourceVariable() = v)\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if `def1` in `bb1` may step to `def2` in `bb2`. */\n    private predicate step(SsaDefinition def1, BasicBlock bb1, SsaDefinition def2, BasicBlock bb2) {\n      not sinkBlock(def1, bb1, _) and\n      not Config::barrierEdge(bb1, bb2) and\n      not ssaValueBarrierEdge(def1, bb1, bb2) and\n      (\n        def2.(SsaPhiDefinition).hasInputFromBlock(def1, bb1) and bb2 = def2.getBasicBlock()\n        or\n        exists(SourceVariable v |\n          ssaRelevantAtEndOfBlock(def1, bb1) and\n          bb1.getASuccessor() = bb2 and\n          v = def1.getSourceVariable() and\n          not phiBlock(bb2, v) and\n          def1 = def2\n        )\n        or\n        uncertainStep(def1, def2) and\n        bb2 = def2.getBasicBlock() and\n        bb1 = bb2\n      )\n    }\n\n    bindingset[bb1, bb2, fs1]\n    pragma[inline_late]\n    private predicate stepFinallyStack(\n      BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, FinallyStack fs1, FinallyStack fs2\n    ) {\n      exists(boolean abrupt | entersFinally(bb1, bb2, abrupt, _) and fs2 = fs1.enter(abrupt)) and\n      not leavesFinally(bb1, bb2, _, _)\n      or\n      exists(boolean abrupt | leavesFinally(bb1, bb2, abrupt, _) and fs2 = fs1.leave(abrupt)) and\n      not entersFinally(bb1, bb2, _, _)\n      or\n      exists(boolean abrupt |\n        leavesFinally(bb1, bb2, abrupt, _) and\n        entersFinally(bb1, bb2, abrupt, _) and\n        fs2 = fs1.leave(abrupt).enter(abrupt)\n      )\n      or\n      not entersFinally(bb1, bb2, _, _) and not leavesFinally(bb1, bb2, _, _) and fs2 = fs1\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the source `srcDef` in `srcBb` may reach `def` in `bb`. If the\n     * path has entered one or more finally blocks then `fs` tracks the\n     * `SuccessorType`s of the edges entering those blocks.\n     */\n    private predicate sourceReachesBlock(\n      SsaDefinition srcDef, BasicBlock srcBb, SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb, FinallyStack fs\n    ) {\n      sourceBlock(srcDef, srcBb, _) and\n      def = srcDef and\n      bb = srcBb and\n      fs = TNil()\n      or\n      exists(SsaDefinition middef, BasicBlock midbb, FinallyStack midfs |\n        sourceReachesBlock(srcDef, srcBb, middef, midbb, midfs) and\n        step(middef, midbb, def, bb) and\n        stepFinallyStack(midbb, bb, midfs, fs)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `def` in `bb` is reachable from a source and may reach a sink.\n     */\n    private predicate blockReachesSink(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb) {\n      sourceReachesBlock(_, _, def, bb, _) and\n      (\n        sinkBlock(def, bb, _)\n        or\n        exists(SsaDefinition middef, BasicBlock midbb |\n          step(def, bb, middef, midbb) and\n          blockReachesSink(middef, midbb)\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate escapeCandidate(SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb) {\n      sourceBlock(def, bb, _)\n      or\n      exists(SsaDefinition middef, BasicBlock midbb |\n        blockReachesSink(middef, midbb) and\n        step(middef, midbb, def, bb)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the source `srcDef` in `srcBb` may reach `escDef` in `escBb` and from\n     * there cannot reach a sink.\n     */\n    private predicate sourceEscapesSink(\n      SsaDefinition srcDef, BasicBlock srcBb, SsaDefinition escDef, BasicBlock escBb\n    ) {\n      sourceReachesBlock(srcDef, srcBb, escDef, escBb, _) and\n      escapeCandidate(escDef, escBb) and\n      not blockReachesSink(escDef, escBb)\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if `bb` is a relevant block for computing reachability of `src`. */\n    private predicate pathBlock(SourceVariable src, BasicBlock bb) {\n      exists(SsaDefinition def | def.getSourceVariable() = src |\n        blockReachesSink(def, bb)\n        or\n        escapeCandidate(def, bb)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `bb1` to `bb2` is a relevant edge for computing reachability\n     * of `src`.\n     */\n    private predicate pathEdge(SourceVariable src, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2) {\n      step(_, bb1, _, bb2) and\n      pathBlock(pragma[only_bind_into](src), bb1) and\n      pathBlock(pragma[only_bind_into](src), bb2) and\n      bb1 != bb2\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the edge from `bb1` to `bb2` implies that `def` has the value\n     * `gv` and that the edge is relevant for computing reachability of `src`.\n     *\n     * If multiple values may be implied by this edge, including a singleton,\n     * then we only include the singleton.\n     *\n     * The underlying variable of `t` is `var`.\n     */\n    private predicate ssaControlsPathEdge(\n      SourceVariable src, SsaDefinition t, SourceVariable var, GuardValue gv, BasicBlock bb1,\n      BasicBlock bb2\n    ) {\n      ssaControlsBranchEdge(t, bb1, bb2, gv) and\n      (\n        any(GuardValue gv0 | ssaControlsBranchEdge(t, bb1, bb2, gv0)).isSingleton()\n        implies\n        gv.isSingleton()\n      ) and\n      pathEdge(src, bb1, bb2) and\n      t.getSourceVariable() = var\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the reachability path for `src` may go through a loop with\n     * entry point `entry`.\n     */\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate loopEntryBlock(SourceVariable src, BasicBlock entry) {\n      exists(BasicBlock pred | pathEdge(src, pred, entry) and entry.strictlyDominates(pred))\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets either `gv` or its dual value. This is intended as a mostly unique\n     * representation of the set of values `gv` and `gv.getDualValue()`.\n     */\n    private GuardValue getPrimary(GuardValue gv) {\n      exists(GuardValue dual | dual = gv.getDualValue() |\n        if dual.isSingleton() then result = dual else result = gv\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if precision may be improved by splitting control flow on the\n     * value of `var` during the reachability computation of `src`.\n     *\n     * The `condgv`/`condgv.getDualValue()` separation of the values of `var`\n     * determines whether a possibly relevant edge may be taken or not.\n     */\n    private predicate relevantSplit(SourceVariable src, SourceVariable var, GuardValue condgv) {\n      // `var` may be a relevant split if we encounter 2+ conditional edges\n      // that imply information about `var`.\n      exists(GuardValue gv |\n        ssaControlsPathEdge(src, _, var, gv, _, _) and\n        condgv = getPrimary(gv) and\n        2 <= strictcount(BasicBlock bb1 | ssaControlsPathEdge(src, _, var, _, bb1, _))\n      )\n      or\n      // Or if we encounter a conditional edge that imply a value that's\n      // incompatible with an initial or later assigned value.\n      exists(GuardValue gv1, GuardValue gv2, BasicBlock bb |\n        condgv = getPrimary(gv1) and\n        ssaControlsPathEdge(src, _, var, gv1, _, _) and\n        initSsaValue(var, bb, _, gv2) and\n        disjointValues(gv1, gv2) and\n        pathBlock(src, bb)\n      )\n      or\n      // Or if we encounter a conditional edge in a loop that imply a value for\n      // `var` that may be unchanged from one iteration to the next.\n      exists(\n        SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, BasicBlock loopEntry, GuardValue gv\n      |\n        ssaControlsPathEdge(src, def, var, gv, bb1, bb2) and\n        condgv = getPrimary(gv) and\n        loopEntryBlock(src, loopEntry) and\n        loopEntry.strictlyDominates(bb1) and\n        bb2.getASuccessor*() = loopEntry\n      |\n        def.getBasicBlock().dominates(loopEntry)\n        or\n        exists(SsaPhiDefinition phi |\n          phi.definesAt(var, loopEntry, _) and\n          phi.getAnInput+() = def and\n          def.(SsaPhiDefinition).getAnInput*() = phi\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    private module SsaDefOption = Option<SsaDefinition>;\n\n    private class SsaDefOption = SsaDefOption::Option;\n\n    private predicate lastDefInBlock(SourceVariable var, SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb) {\n      def = max(SsaDefinition d, int i | d.definesAt(var, bb, i) | d order by i)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `gv` is relatable to the `condgv`/`condgv.getDualValue()` pair\n     * in the sense that a conditional branch based on `condgv` may be\n     * determined by `gv`.\n     */\n    bindingset[gv, condgv]\n    pragma[inline_late]\n    private predicate relatable(GuardValue gv, GuardValue condgv) {\n      disjointValues(gv, condgv) or\n      disjointValues(gv, condgv.getDualValue())\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `bb1` to `bb2` is a relevant edge for computing reachability of\n     * `src`, and `var` is a relevant splitting variable that gets (re-)defined\n     * in `bb2` by `t`, which is not a phi node.\n     *\n     * `val` is the best known value that is relatable to `condgv` for `t` in `bb2`.\n     */\n    private predicate stepSsaValueRedef(\n      SourceVariable src, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, SourceVariable var, GuardValue condgv,\n      SsaDefinition t, GuardValueOption val\n    ) {\n      pathEdge(src, bb1, bb2) and\n      relevantSplit(src, var, condgv) and\n      lastDefInBlock(var, t, bb2) and\n      not t instanceof SsaPhiDefinition and\n      (\n        exists(GuardValue gv |\n          ssaHasValue(t, gv) and\n          if relatable(gv, condgv) then val.asSome() = gv else val.isNone()\n        )\n        or\n        not ssaHasValue(t, _) and val.isNone()\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `bb1` to `bb2` is a relevant edge for computing reachability of\n     * `src`, and `var` is a relevant splitting variable that has a phi node,\n     * `t2`, in `bb2` taking input from `t1` along this edge. Furthermore,\n     * there is no further redefinition of `var` in `bb2`.\n     *\n     * `val` is the best value that is relatable to `condgv` for `t1`/`t2`\n     * implied by taking this edge.\n     */\n    private predicate stepSsaValuePhi(\n      SourceVariable src, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, SourceVariable var, GuardValue condgv,\n      SsaDefinition t1, SsaDefinition t2, GuardValueOption val\n    ) {\n      pathEdge(src, bb1, bb2) and\n      relevantSplit(src, var, condgv) and\n      lastDefInBlock(var, t2, bb2) and\n      t2.(SsaPhiDefinition).hasInputFromBlock(t1, bb1) and\n      (\n        exists(GuardValue gv |\n          ssaControlsPathEdge(src, t1, _, gv, bb1, bb2) and\n          if relatable(gv, condgv) then val.asSome() = gv else val.isNone()\n        )\n        or\n        not ssaControlsPathEdge(src, t1, _, _, bb1, bb2) and\n        val.isNone()\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if `bb1` to `bb2` is a relevant edge for computing reachability of\n     * `src`, and `var` is a relevant splitting variable that has no\n     * redefinition along this edge nor in `bb2`.\n     *\n     * Additionally, this edge implies that the SSA definition `t` of `var` has\n     * value `val` and that `val` is relatable to `condgv`.\n     */\n    private predicate stepSsaValueNoRedef(\n      SourceVariable src, BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, SourceVariable var, GuardValue condgv,\n      SsaDefinition t, GuardValue val\n    ) {\n      pathEdge(src, bb1, bb2) and\n      relevantSplit(src, var, condgv) and\n      not lastDefInBlock(var, _, bb2) and\n      ssaControlsPathEdge(src, t, var, val, bb1, bb2) and\n      relatable(val, condgv)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the source `srcDef` in `srcBb` may reach `def` in `bb`. The\n     * taken path takes splitting based on the value of `var` into account.\n     *\n     * When multiple `GuardValue`s can be chosen for `var`, we prioritize those\n     * that are relatable to `condgv`, as that will help determine whether a\n     * particular edge may be taken or not. Singleton values are prioritized\n     * highly as they are in principle relatable to every other `GuardValue`.\n     *\n     * The pair `(tracked, val)` is the current SSA definition and known value\n     * for `var` in `bb`.\n     */\n    private predicate sourceReachesBlockWithTrackedVar(\n      SsaDefinition srcDef, BasicBlock srcBb, SsaDefinition def, BasicBlock bb, FinallyStack fs,\n      SsaDefOption tracked, GuardValueOption val, SourceVariable var, GuardValue condgv\n    ) {\n      sourceBlock(srcDef, srcBb, _) and\n      def = srcDef and\n      bb = srcBb and\n      fs = TNil() and\n      relevantSplit(def.getSourceVariable(), var, condgv) and\n      (\n        // tracking variable is not yet live\n        not ssaLiveAtEndOfBlock(var, _, bb) and\n        tracked.isNone() and\n        val.isNone()\n        or\n        // tracking variable is live but without known value\n        ssaLiveAtEndOfBlock(var, tracked.asSome(), bb) and\n        not initSsaValue(var, bb, _, _) and\n        val.isNone()\n        or\n        // tracking variable has known value, track it if it is relatable to condgv\n        exists(GuardValue gv | initSsaValue(var, bb, tracked.asSome(), gv) |\n          if relatable(gv, condgv) then val.asSome() = gv else val.isNone()\n        )\n      )\n      or\n      exists(\n        SourceVariable src, SsaDefinition middef, BasicBlock midbb, FinallyStack midfs,\n        SsaDefOption tracked0, GuardValueOption val0\n      |\n        sourceReachesBlockWithTrackedVar(srcDef, srcBb, middef, midbb, midfs, tracked0, val0, var,\n          condgv) and\n        src = srcDef.getSourceVariable() and\n        step(middef, midbb, def, bb) and\n        stepFinallyStack(midbb, bb, midfs, fs) and\n        pathBlock(pragma[only_bind_into](src), bb) and\n        not exists(GuardValue gv |\n          ssaControlsPathEdge(src, tracked0.asSome(), _, gv, midbb, bb) and\n          disjointValues(val0.asSome(), gv)\n        )\n      |\n        // tracking variable is redefined\n        stepSsaValueRedef(src, midbb, bb, var, condgv, tracked.asSome(), val)\n        or\n        exists(GuardValueOption val1 |\n          // tracking variable has a phi node, and maybe value information from the edge\n          stepSsaValuePhi(src, midbb, bb, var, condgv, tracked0.asSome(), tracked.asSome(), val1)\n        |\n          val = val0 and val1.isNone()\n          or\n          val = intersect(val0, val1.asSome())\n        )\n        or\n        exists(GuardValue val1 |\n          // tracking variable is unchanged, and has value information from the edge\n          stepSsaValueNoRedef(src, midbb, bb, var, condgv, tracked0.asSome(), val1) and\n          tracked = tracked0 and\n          val = intersect(val0, val1)\n        )\n        or\n        // tracking variable is unchanged, and has no value information from the edge\n        not lastDefInBlock(var, _, bb) and\n        not stepSsaValueNoRedef(src, midbb, bb, var, condgv, tracked0.asSome(), _) and\n        tracked = tracked0 and\n        val = val0\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the source `srcDef` at `src` may reach the sink `sinkDef` at `sink`.\n     */\n    predicate flow(\n      ControlFlowNode src, SsaDefinition srcDef, ControlFlowNode sink, SsaDefinition sinkDef\n    ) {\n      intraBlockFlow(src, srcDef, sink, sinkDef)\n      or\n      exists(BasicBlock srcBb, BasicBlock sinkBb, SourceVariable srcVar |\n        sourceBlock(srcDef, srcBb, src) and\n        sourceReachesBlock(srcDef, srcBb, sinkDef, sinkBb, _) and\n        sinkBlock(sinkDef, sinkBb, sink) and\n        srcVar = srcDef.getSourceVariable() and\n        forall(SourceVariable t, GuardValue condgv | relevantSplit(srcVar, t, condgv) |\n          sourceReachesBlockWithTrackedVar(srcDef, srcBb, sinkDef, sinkBb, _, _, _, t, condgv)\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the source `srcDef` at `src` may escape, that is, there It may also be a switch case, which as a guard is considered\n   * to evaluate to either true or false depending on whether the case matches.\n   */\n  final class PreGuard extends FinalAstNode {\n    /**\n     * Holds if this guard evaluating to `v` corresponds to taking the edge\n     * from `bb1` to `bb2`. For ordinary conditional branching this guard is\n     * the last node in `bb1`, but for switch case matching it is the switch\n     * expression, which may either be in `bb1` or an earlier basic block.\n     */\n    predicate hasValueBranchEdge(BasicBlock bb1, BasicBlock bb2, GuardValue v) {\n      bb1.getLastNode() = this.(Expr).getControlFlowNode() and\n      branchEdge(bb1, bb2, v)\n      or\n      caseBranchEdge(bb1, bb2, v, this)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this guard evaluating to `v` directly controls the basic block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, `bb` is dominated by the `v`-successor edge of this guard.\n     */\n    predicate directlyValueControls(BasicBlock bb, GuardValue v) {\n      exists(BasicBlock guard, BasicBlock succ |\n        this.hasValueBranchEdge(guard, succ, v) and\n        dominatingEdge(guard, succ) and\n        succ.dominates(bb)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this guard is the last node in `bb1` and that its successor is\n     * gv.asBooleanValue() = branch))\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this guard evaluating to `branch` directly controls the basic\n     * block `bb`.\n     *\n     * That is, `bb` is dominated by the `branch`-successor edge of this guard.\n     */\n    predicate directlyControls(BasicBlock bb, boolean branch) {\n      this.directlyValueControls(bb, any(GuardValue gv | gv.asBooleanValue() = branch))\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if this guard tests equality between `e1` and `e2` upon evaluating\n     * to `eqval`.\n     */\n    predicate isEquality(Expr e1, Expr e2, boolean eqval) {\n      equalityTestSymmetric(this, e1, e2, eqval)\n      or\n      constcaseEquality(this, e1, e2) and eqval = true\n      or\n      constcaseEquality(this, e2, e1) and eqval = true\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets the basic block of this guard. For expressions, this is the basic\n     * block of the expression itself, and for switch cases, this is the basic\n     * block of the expression being compared against the cases.\n     */\n    BasicBlock getBasicBlock() {\n      result = this.(Expr).getBasicBlock()\n      or\n      result = this.(Case).getSwitchExpr().getBasicBlock()\n    }\n  }\n\n  private Expr getBranchExpr(ConditionalExpr cond, boolean branch) {\n    branch = true and result = cond.getThen()\n    or\n    branch = false and result = cond.getElse()\n  }\n\n  private predicate baseImpliesStep(PreGuard g1, GuardValue v1, PreGuard g2, GuardValue v2) {\n    g1.(AndExpr).getAnOperand() = g2 and v1.asBooleanValue() = true and v2 = v1\n    or\n    g1.(OrExpr).getAnOperand() = g2 and v1.asBooleanValue() = false and v2 = v1\n    or\n    g1.(NotExpr).getOperand() = g2 and v1.asBooleanValue().booleanNot() = v2.asBooleanValue()\n    or\n    exists(GuardValue eqval, ConstantExpr constant, GuardValue cv |\n      g1.isEquality(g2, constant, eqval.asBooleanValue()) and\n      constantHasValue(constant, cv)\n    |\n      v1 = eqval and v2 = cv\n      or\n      v1 = eqval.getDualValue() and v2 = cv.getDualValue()\n    )\n    or\n    exists(NonNullExpr nonnull |\n      equalityTestSymmetric(g1, g2, nonnull, v1.asBooleanValue()) and\n      v2.isNonNullValue() and\n      not g2 instanceof NonNullExpr // disregard trivial guard\n    )\n    or\n    exists(Case c1, Expr switchExpr |\n      g1 = c1 and\n      c1.isDefaultCase() and\n      c1.getSwitchExpr() = switchExpr and\n      v1.asBooleanValue() = true and\n      g2.(Case).getSwitchExpr() = switchExpr and\n      v2.asBooleanValue() = false and\n      g1 != g2\n    )\n  }\n\n  private predicate normalExitBlock(BasicBlock bb) { bb.getNode(_) instanceof NormalExitNode }\n\n  signature module LogicInputSig {\n    class SsaDefinition {\n      /** Gets the basic block to which this SSA definition impliesStep1(Guard g1, GuardValue v1, Guard g2, GuardValue v2) {\n      baseImpliesStep(g1, v1, g2, v2)\n      or\n      exists(SsaDefinition def, Expr e, BasicBlock bb1 |\n        // If `def = g2 ?    /*\n     * Stores into closure aliases block flow from previous stores, both to\n     * avoid overlapping data flow paths, but also to avoid false positive\n     * flow.\n     *\n     * Example 1 (\n                // When there are both sources and sinks in the diff range,\n                // diff-informed dataflow falls back to computing all paths without\n                // any filtering. To prevent significant alert flip-flopping due to\n                // minor code changes triggering the fallback, we consistently apply\n                // source-or-sink filtering here to ensure that we return the same\n                // paths regardless of whether the fallback is triggered.\n                if Config::observeDiffInformedIncrementalMode()\n                then private module AlertFiltering = AlertFilteringImpl<Location>;\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if the given node is visible in overlay-only local evaluation.\n       *\n       * This predicate needs to be `overlay[local?]`, either directly or\n       * through annotations from an outer scope. If `Node` is global for the\n       * language under analysis, then every node is considered an overlay\n       * node, which means there will effectively be no overlay-based\n       * filtering of sources and sinks.\n       */\n      private predicate isOverlayNode(Node node) {\n        isEvaluatingInOverlay() and\n        // Any local node is an overlay node if we are evaluating in overlay mode\n        exists(node)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * The filtering if we aren't meant to be diff-informed.\n       *\n       * Shared between sources and sinks.\n       */\n      overlay[global]\n      pragma[inline]\n      private predicate nonDiffInformedFilter(Node node) {\n        // If we are in base-only global evaluation, do not filter out any sources/sinks.\n        not isEvaluatingInOverlay()\n        or\n        // If the configuration doesn't merge overlays, do not filter out any sources/sinks.\n        not Config::observeOverlayInformedIncrementalMode()\n        or\n        // If we are in global evaluation with an overlay present, restrict\n        // sources/sinks to those visible in the overlay.\n        isOverlayNode(node)\n      }\n\n      overlay[global]\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      private predicate isFilteredSource(Node source) {\n        Config::isSource(source, _) and\n        // Data flow is always incremental in one of two ways.\n        // 1. If the configuration is diff-informed, we filter to only include nodes in the diff,\n        //    which gives the smallest set of nodes.\n        //    If diff information is not available, we do not filter at all.\n        // 2. If not, in global evaluation with overlay, we filter to only\n        //    include nodes from files in the overlay; flow from\n        //    other nodes will be added back later.\n        // We start by seeing if we should be in case 1.\n        if Config::observeDiffInformedIncrementalMode()\n        then\n          // Case 1: We are meant to be diff-informed.\n          // We still only filter if we have diff information.\n          AlertFiltering::diffInformationAvailable()\n          implies\n          AlertFiltering::locationIsInDiff(Config::getASelectedSourceLocation(source))\n        else nonDiffInformedFilter(source)\n      }\n\n      overlay[global]\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      private predicate isFilteredSink(Node sink) {\n        (\n          Config::isSink(sink, _) or\n          Config::isSink(sink)\n        ) and\n        // See the comments in `isFilteredSource` for the reasoning behind the following.\n        if Config::observeDiffInformedIncrementalMode()\n        then\n          AlertFiltering::diffInformationAvailable()\n          implies\n          AlertFiltering::locationIsInDiff(Config::getASelectedSinkLocation(sink))\n        else nonDiffInformedFilter(sink)\n      }\n\n      private predicate hasFilteredSource() { isFilteredSource(_) }\n\n      private predicate hasFilteredSink() { isFilteredSink(_) }\n\n      predicate isRelevantSource(Node source, FlowState state) {\n        // If there are filtered sinks, we need to pass through all sources to preserve all alerts\n        // with filtered sinks. Otherwise the only alerts of interest are those with filtered\n        // sources, so we can perform the source filtering right here.\n        Config::isSource(source, state) and\n        (\n          isFilteredSource(source) or\n          hasFilteredSink()\n        )\n      }\n\n      predicate isRelevantSink(Node sink, FlowState state) {\n        // If there are filtered sources, we need to pass through all sinks to preserve all alerts\n        // with filtered sources. Otherwise the only alerts of interest are those with filtered\n        // sinks, so we can perform the sink filtering right here.\n        Config::isSink(sink, state) and\n        (\n          isFilteredSink(sink) or\n          hasFilteredSource()\n        )\n      }\n\n      predicate isRelevantSink(Node sink) {\n        // If there are filtered sources, we need to pass through all sinks to preserve all alerts\n        // with filtered sources. Otherwise the only alerts of interest are those with filtered\n        // sinks, so we can perform the sink filtering right here.\n        Config::isSink(sink) and\n        (\n          isFilteredSink(sink) or\n          hasFilteredSource()\n        )\n      }\n\n      bindingset[source, sink]\n      pragma[inline_late]\n      predicate isRelevantSourceSinkPair(Node source, Node sink) {\n        isFilteredSource(source) or\n        isFilteredSink(sink)\n      }\n    }\n\n    private import SourceSinkFiltering\n\n    private predicate inBarrier(NodeEx node) {\n isRelevantSink(n)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate outBarrier(NodeEx node, FlowState state) {\n      exists(Node n |\n        node.asNodeOrImplicitRead() = n and\n
