   exists(SummaryComponent head0, SummaryComponentStack tail0 |\n        derivedFluentFlowPush(c, input, arg, head0, tail0, i + 1) and\n        head = arg.drop(i).head() and\n        tail = SummaryComponentStack::push(head0, tail0)\n      )\n    }\n\n    private predicate isCallbackParameter(SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      s.head() = TParameterSummaryComponent(_) and exists(s.tail())\n    }\n\n    private predicate isContentOfArgument(SummaryComponentStack s, ParameterPosition pos) {\n      s.head() = TContentSummaryComponent(_) and isContentOfArgument(s.tail(), pos)\n      or\n      s = SummaryComponentStack::argument(pos)\n    }\n\n    private predicate outputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      summary(c, _, s, _, _)\n      or\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack out |\n        outputState(c, out) and\n        out.head() = TContentSummaryComponent(_) and\n        s = out.tail()\n      )\n      or\n      // Add the argument node corresponding to the requested post-update node\n      inputState(c, s) and isCallbackParameter(s)\n    }\n\n    private predicate inputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      summary(c, s, _, _, _)\n      or\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack inp | inputState(c, inp) and s = inp.tail())\n      or\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack out |\n        outputState(c, out) and\n        out.head() = TParameterSummaryComponent(_) and\n        s = out.tail()\n      )\n      or\n      // Add the post-update node corresponding to the requested argument node\n      outputState(c, s) and isCallbackParameter(s)\n      or\n      // Add the parameter node for parameter side-effects\n      outputState(c, s) and s = SummaryComponentStack::argument(_)\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate sourceOutputStateEntry(\n      SourceElement source, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n    ) {\n      exists(string outSpec |\n        source.isSource(outSpec, kind, _, model) and\n        External::interpretSpec(outSpec, s)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate sourceOutputState(\n      SourceElement source, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n    ) {\n      sourceOutputStateEntry(source, s, kind, model)\n      or\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack out |\n        sourceOutputState(source, out, kind, model) and\n        out.head() = TContentSummaryComponent(_) and\n        s = out.tail()\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate sinkInputStateExit(\n      SinkElement sink, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n    ) {\n      exists(string inSpec |\n        sink.isSink(inSpec, kind, _, model) and\n        External::interpretSpec(inSpec, s)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[nomagic]\n    private predicate sinkInputState(\n      SinkElement sink, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n    ) {\n      sinkInputStateExit(sink, s, kind, model)\n      or\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack inp |\n        sinkInputState(sink, inp, kind, model) and\n        inp.head() = TContentSummaryComponent(_) and\n        s = inp.tail()\n      )\n    }\n\n    private newtype TSummaryNodeState =\n      TSummaryNodeInputState(SummaryComponentStack s) { inputState(_, s) } or\n      TSummaryNodeOutputState(SummaryComponentStack s) { outputState(_, s) } or\n      TSourceOutputState(SummaryComponentStack s) { sourceOutputState(_, s, _, _) } or\n      TSinkInputState(SummaryComponentStack s) { sinkInputState(_, s, _, _) }\n\n    /**\n     * A state used to break up (complex) flow summaries into atomic flow steps.\n     * For a flow summary\n     *\n     * ```ql\n     * propagatesFlow(\n     *   SummaryComponentStack input, SummaryComponentStack output, boolean preservesValue, string model\n     * )\n     * ```\n     *\n     * the following states are used:\n     *\n     * - `TSummaryNodeInputState(SummaryComponentStack s)`:\n     *   this state represents that the components in `s` _have been read_ from the\n     *   input.\n     * - `TSummaryNodeOutputState(SummaryComponentStack s)`:\n     *   this state represents that the components in `s` _remain to be written_ to\n     *   the output.\n     */\n    private class SummaryNodeState extends TSummaryNodeState {\n      /** Holds if this state is a valid input state for `c`. */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isInputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n        this = TSummaryNodeInputState(s) and\n        inputState(c, s)\n      }\n\n      /** Holds if this state is a valid output state for `c`. */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isOutputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n        this = TSummaryNodeOutputState(s) and\n        outputState(c, s)\n      }\n\n      /** Holds if this state is a valid output state for `source`. */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isSourceOutputState(\n        SourceElement source, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n      ) {\n        sourceOutputState(source, s, kind, model) and\n        this = TSourceOutputState(s)\n      }\n\n      /** Holds if this state is a valid input state for `sink`. */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isSinkInputState(\n        SinkElement sink, SummaryComponentStack s, string kind, string model\n      ) {\n        sinkInputState(sink, s, kind, model) and\n        this = TSinkInputState(s)\n      }\n\n      /** Gets a textual representation of this state. */\n      string toString() {\n        exists(SummaryComponentStack s |\n          this = TSummaryNodeInputState(s) and\n          result = \"read: \" + s\n        )\n        or\n        exists(SummaryComponentStack s |\n          this = TSummaryNodeOutputState(s) and\n          result = \"to write: \" + s\n        )\n        or\n        exists(SummaryComponentStack s |\n          this = TSourceOutputState(s) and\n          result = \"to write source: \" + s\n        )\n        or\n        exists(SummaryComponentStack s |\n          this = TSinkInputState(s) and\n          result = \"read sink: \" + s\n        )\n      }\n    }\n\n    private newtype TSummaryNode =\n      TSummaryInternalNode(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryNodeState state) {\n        summaryNodeRange(c, state)\n      } or\n      TSummaryParameterNode(SummarizedCallable c, ParameterPosition pos) {\n        summaryParameterNodeRange(c, pos)\n      } or\n      TSourceOutputNode(SourceElement source, SummaryNodeState state, string kind, string model) {\n        state.isSourceOutputState(source, _, kind, model)\n      } or\n      TSinkInputNode(SinkElement sink, SummaryNodeState state, string kind, string model) {\n        state.isSinkInputState(sink, _, kind, model)\n      }\n\n    abstract class SummaryNode extends TSummaryNode {\n      abstract string toString();\n\n      abstract SummarizedCallable getSummarizedCallable();\n\n      abstract SourceElement getSourceElement();\n\n      abstract SinkElement getSinkElement();\n\n      predicate isHidden() { any() }\n    }\n\n    private class SummaryInternalNode extends SummaryNode, TSummaryInternalNode {\n      private SummarizedCallable c;\n      private SummaryNodeState state;\n\n      SummaryInternalNode() { this = TSummaryInternalNode(c, state) }\n\n      override string toString() { result = \"[summary] \" + state + \" in \" + c }\n\n      override SummarizedCallable getSummarizedCallable() { result = c }\n\n      override SourceElement getSourceElement() { none() }\n\n      override SinkElement getSinkElement() { none() }\n    }\n\n    private class SummaryParamNode extends SummaryNode, TSummaryParameterNode {\n      private SummarizedCallable c;\n      private ParameterPosition pos;\n\n      SummaryParamNode() { this = TSummaryParameterNode(c, pos) }\n\n      override string toString() { result = \"[summary param] \" + pos + \" in \" + c }\n\n      override SummarizedCallable getSummarizedCallable() { result = c }\n\n      override SourceElement getSourceElement() { none() }\n\n      override SinkElement getSinkElement() { none() }\n    }\n\n    class SourceOutputNode extends SummaryNode, TSourceOutputNode {\n      private SourceElement source_;\n      private SummaryNodeState state_;\n      private string kind_;\n      private string model_;\n\n      SourceOutputNode() { this = TSourceOutputNode(source_, state_, kind_, model_) }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if this node is an entry node, i.e. before any stores have been performed.\n       *\n       * This node should be used as the actual source node in data flow configurations.\n       */\n      predicate isEntry(string kind, string model) {\n        model = model_ and\n        exists(SummaryComponentStack out |\n          sourceOutputStateEntry(source_, out, kind, model_) and\n          state_.isSourceOutputState(source_, out, kind, model_)\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if this node is an exit node, i.e. after all stores have been performed.\n       *\n       * A local flow step should be added from this node to a data flow node representing\n       * `s` inside `source`.\n       */\n      predicate isExit(SourceElement source, SummaryComponentStack s, string model) {\n        source = source_ and\n        model = model_ and\n        state_.isSourceOutputState(source, s, _, model)\n      }\n\n      override predicate isHidden() { not this.isEntry(_, _) }\n\n      override string toString() {\n        if this.isEntry(_, _)\n        then result = source_.toString()\n        else result = \"[source] \" + state_ + \" at \" + source_\n      }\n\n      override SummarizedCallable getSummarizedCallable() { none() }\n\n      override SourceElement getSourceElement() { result = source_ }\n\n      override SinkElement getSinkElement() { none() }\n    }\n\n    class SinkInputNode extends SummaryNode, TSinkInputNode {\n      private SinkElement sink_;\n      private SummaryNodeState state_;\n      private string kind_;\n      private string model_;\n\n      SinkInputNode() { this = TSinkInputNode(sink_, state_, kind_, model_) }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if this node is an entry node, i.e. before any reads have been performed.\n       *\n       * A local flow step should be added to this node from a data flow node representing\n       * `sc` inside `sink`.\n       */\n      predicate isEntry(SinkElement sink, SummaryComponent sc, string model) {\n        sink = sink_ and\n        model = model_ and\n        state_.isSinkInputState(sink, TSingletonSummaryComponentStack(sc), _, model)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if this node is an exit node, i.e. after all reads have been performed.\n       *\n       * This node should be used as the actual sink node in data flow configurations.\n       */\n      predicate     state_.isSinkInputState(sink_, inp, kind, model_)\n        )\n      }\n\n      override predicate isHidden() { not this.isExit(_, _) }\n\n      override string toString() {\n        if _) and\n      not parameterReadState(c, state, _)\n      or\n      state.isOutputState(c, _)\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private SummaryNode summaryNodeInputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      exists(SummaryNodeState state | state.isInputState(c, s) |\n        result = TSummaryInternalNode(c, state)\n        or\n        exists(ParameterPosition pos |\n          parameterReadState(c, state, pos) and\n          result = TSummaryParameterNode(c, pos)\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private SummaryNode summaryNodeOutputState(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      exists(SummaryNodeState state |\n        state.isOutputState(c, s) and\n        result = TSummaryInternalNode(c, state)\n      )\n    }\n\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private SummaryNode sourceElementOutputState(SourceElement source, SummaryComponentStack s) {\n      exists(SummaryNodeState state, string kind, string model result = TSinkInputNode(sink, state, kind, model)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if a write targets `post`, which is a post-update node for a\n     * parameter at position `pos` in `c`.\n     */\n    private predicate isParameterPostUpdate(\n      SummaryNode post, SummarizedCallable c, ParameterPosition pos\n    ) {\n      post = summaryNodeOutputState(c, SummaryComponentStack::argument(pos))\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if a parameter node at position `pos` is required for `c`. */\n    private predicate summaryParameterNodeRange(SummarizedCallable c, ParameterPosition pos) {\n      parameterReadState(c, _, pos)\n      or\n      // Same as `isParameterPostUpdate(_, c, pos)`, but can be used in a negative context\n      any(SummaryNodeState state).isOutputState(c, SummaryComponentStack::argument(pos))\n    }\n\n    private predicate callbackOutput(\n      SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s, SummaryNode receiver, ReturnKind rk\n    ) {\n      any(SummaryNodeState state).isInputState(c, s) and\n      s.head() = TReturnSummaryComponent(rk) and\n      receiver = summaryNodeInputState(c, s.tail())\n    }\n\n    private predicate callbackInput(\n      SummarizedCallable c, SummaryComponentStack s, SummaryNode receiver, ArgumentPosition pos\n    ) {\n      any(SummaryNodeState state).isOutputState(c, s) and\n      s.head() = TParameterSummaryComponent(pos) and\n      receiver = summaryNodeInputState(c, s.tail())\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if a call targeting `receiver` should be synthesized inside `c`. */\n    predicate summaryCallbackRange(SummarizedCallable c, SummaryNode receiver) {\n      callbackOutput(c, _, receiver, _)\n      or\n      callbackInput(c, _, receiver, _)\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if SummaryComponentStack s |\n        callbackInput(callable, s, _, _) and\n        pre = summaryNodeOutputState(callable, s) and\n        post = summaryNodeInputState(callable, s)\n      )\n    }\n\n    /** Holds if summary node `ret` is a return node of kind `rk`. */\n    predicate summaryReturnNode(SummaryNode ret, ReturnKind rk) {\n      exists(SummaryComponentStack s |\n        ret = StepsInputSig {\n      /** Gets a call that targets summarized callable `sc`. */\n      DataFlowCall getACall(SummarizedCallable sc);\n\n      /** Gets the enclosing callable of `source`. */\n StepsInput> {\n      /**\n       * Holds if there is a local step from `pred` to `succ`, which is synthesized\n       * from a flow summary.\n       */\n      predicate summaryLocalStep(\n /**\n       * Holds if there is a read step of content `c` from `pred` to `succ`, which\n       * is synthesized from a flow summary.\n       */\n      predicate summaryReadStep(SummaryNode pred, predicate sourceJumpStep(SourceOutputNode nodeFrom, Node nodeTo) {\n        sourceStep(nodeFrom, nodeTo, _, false)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if values stored inside content `c` are cleared at `n`. `n` is a\n       * synthesized summary node, so in order for values to be cleared at calls\n       * to the relevant method, it is important that flow does not pass over\n       * the argument, either via use-use flow or def-use flow.\n       *\n       * Example:\n       *\n       * ```\n       * a.b = taint;\n       * a.clearB(); // assume we have a flow summary for `clearB` that clears `b` on the qualifier\n       * sink(a.b);\n       * ```\n       *\n       * In the above, flow should not pass from `a` on the first line (or the second\n       * line) to `a` on the third value = Input::locationToFileBaseNameAndLineNumberString(node.getLocation()) // node.getLocation().toString()\n      or\n      // Known unknown edges should be reported as properties rather than edges\n      node = node.getChild(key) and\n      value = \"<unknown>\"\n      or\n      // Report properties\n      value = getPropertyAsGraphString(node, key, node.getLocation())\n    )\n  }\n\n  predicate edges_graph_impl(NodeBase source, NodeBase target, string key, string value) {\n    key = \"semmle.label\" and\n    exists(NodeBase directTarget |\n      directTarget = source.getChild(value) and\n      // [NodeA] ---Input--> [Passthrough] ---Source---> [NodeB]\n      // should get reported as [NodeA] ---Input--> [NodeB]\n      if isPassthroughNode(directTarget)\n      then target = getPassthroughNodeChild(directTarget)\n      else target = directTarget\n    ) and\n    // Known unknowns are reported as properties rather than edges\n    not source = target\n  }\n\n /**\n   * An `ArtifactConsumer` represents an element in code that consumes an artifact.\n   *\n   * The concept of \"`ArtifactConsumer` = `ArtifactNode`\" should be used for inputs, as a consumer can be directly tied\n   * to the artifact it receives, thereby becoming the definitive contextual source for that artifact.\n   *\n   * Architectural Implications:\n   *   * By directly coupling a consumer with the node that receives an artifact, no modeling considerations have to be made\n   *     to provide an interface for identifying the source via the consumer data-flow mechanisms.\n   *   * An artifact's properties (such as being a nonce) are not necessarily inherent; they are determined by the context in which the artifact is consumed.\n   *     The consumer node is therefore essential in defining these properties for inputs.\n   *   * This approach reduces ambiguity by avoiding separate notions of \"artifact source\" and \"consumer\", as the node itself encapsulates both roles.\n   *   * Instances of nodes do not necessarily have to come from a consumer, allowing additional modeling of an artifact to occur outside of the consumer.\n   */\n  abstract class ArtifactConsumer extends ConsumerElement {\n    /**\n     * Use `getAKnownArtifactSource() instead. The behavior of these two predicates is equivalent.\n     */\n    final override KnownElement getAKnownSource() { result = this.getAKnownArtifactSource() }\n\n    final ArtifactInstance getAKnownArtifactSource() { result.flowsTo(this) }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * An `ArtifactConsumer` that is also an `ArtifactInstance`.\n   *\n   * For example:\n   * A `NonceArtifactConsumer` is always the `NonceArtifactInstance` itself, since data only becomes (i.e., is determined to be)\n   * a `NonceArtifactInstance` when it is consumed in a context that expects a nonce (e.g., an argument expecting nonce data).\n   *\n   * In this case, the artifact (nonce) is fully defined by the context in which it is consumed, and the consumer embodies\n   * that identity without the need for additional differentiation. The latter\n * category includes array lengths that are not SSA variables.\n *\n * If an inferred bound relies directly on a condition, then this condition is\n * reported as the reason for the bound.\n */\noverlay[local?]\nmodule;\n\n/*\n * This library tackles range analysis as a flow problem. Consider e.g.:\n * ```\n *   len = arr.length;\n *   if (x < len) { ... y = x-1; ... y ... }\n * ```\n * In this case we would like to infer `y <= arr.length - 2`, and this is\n * accomplished by tracking the bound through a sequence of steps:\n * ```\n *   arr.length --> len = .. --> x < len --> x-1 --> y = .. --> y\n * ```\n *\n * In its simplest form the step relation `E1 --> E2` relates two expressions\n * such that `E1 <= B` implies `E2 <= B` for any `B` (with a second separate\n * step relation handling lower bounds). Examples of such steps include\n * assignments `E2 = E1` and conditions `x <= E1` where `E2` is a use of `x`\n * guarded by the condition.\n *\n * In order to handle subtractions and additions with constants, and strict\n * comparisons, the step relation is augmented with an integer delta. With this\n * generalization `E1 --(delta)--> E2` relates two expressions and an integer\n * such that `E1 <= B` implies `E2 <= B + delta` for any `B`. This corresponds\n * to the predicate `boundFlowStep`.\n *\n * The complete range analysis is then implemented as the transitive closure of\n * the step relation summing the deltas along the way. If `E1` transitively\n * steps to `E2`, `delta` is the sum of deltas along the path, and `B` is an\n * interesting bound equal to the value of `E1` then `E2 <= B + delta`. This\n * corresponds to the predicate `bounded`.\n *\n * Phi nodes need a little bit of extra handling. Consider `x0 = phi(x1, x2)`.\n * There are essentially two cases:\n * - If `x1 <= B + d1` and `x2 <= B + d2` then `x0 <= B + max(d1,d2)`.\n * - If `x1 <= B + d1` and `x2 <= x0 + d2` with `d2 <= 0` then `x0 <= B + d1`.\n * The first case is for whenever a bound can be proven without taking looping\n * into account. The second case is relevant when `x2` comes from a back-edge\n * where we can prove that the variable has been non-increasing through the\n * loop-iteration as this means that any upper bound that holds prior to the\n * loop also holds for the variable during the loop.\n * This generalizes to a phi node with `n` inputs, so if\n * `x0 = phi(x1, ..., xn)` and `xi <= B + delta` for one of the x =(mod) v2 - v1`. By choosing `k =(mod) v2 - v1` with\n      // `0 <= k < mod` we get `k <= y - x`. If the resulting comparison is\n      // strict then the strengthening amount is instead `k - 1` modulo `mod`:\n      // `x < y` means `0 <= y - x - 1 =(mod) k - 1` so `k - 1 <= y - x - 1` and\n      // thus `k - 1 < y - x` with `0 <= k - 1 < mod`.\n      exprModulus(comp.getLesserOperand(), b, v1, mod1) and\n      exprModulus(comp.getGreaterOperand(), b, v2, mod2) and\n      mod = mod1.gcd(mod2) and\n      mod != 1 and\n      (testIsTrue = true or testIsTrue = false) and\n      (\n        if comp.isStrict()\n        then resultIsStrict = testIsTrue\n        else resultIsStrict = testIsTrue.booleanNot()\n      ) and\n      (\n        resultIsStrict = true and d = 1\n        or\n        resultIsStrict = false and d = 0\n      ) and\n      (\n        testIsTrue = true and k = v2 - 1`.\n      (\n        resultIsStrict = true and d3 = strengthen\n        or\n        resultIsStrict = false and d3 = 0\n      ) and\n      delta = D::fromFloat(D::toFloat(d1) + d2 + d3)\n    )\n    or\n    result = eqFlowCond(v, e, delta, true, testIsTrue) and\n    (upper = true or upper = false)\n    or\n    // guard that tests whether `v2` is bounded by `e + delta - }\n\n  /** Holds if `e >= 1` as determined by sign analysis. */\n  private predicate strictlyPositiveIntegralExpr(Sem::Expr e) {\n    semStrictlyPositive(e) and Sem::getExprType(e) instanceof   e2.(Sem::MulExpr).hasOperands(e1, c) and factor = D::fromInt(k)\n      or\n      exists(Sem::ShiftLeftExpr e |\n        e = e2 and\n        e.getLeftOperand() = e1 and\n        e.getRightOperand() = )\n    or\n    exists(D::Delta d, SemReason r1, SemReason r2 |\n      boundedSsa(v, b, d, pos, upper, fromBackEdge, origdelta, r2)\n      or\n      boundedPhi(v, b, d, upper, fromBackEdge, origdelta, NSS 2013.\n *     (https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0849)\n *   Asiri Rathnayake, Hayo Thielecke: Static Analysis for Regular Expression\n *     Exponential Runtime via Substructural Logics. 2014.\n *     (https://www.cs.bham.ac.uk/~hxt/research/redos_full.pdf)\n *\n * The basic idea is to search for overlapping cycles in the NFA, that is,\n * states `q` such that there are two distinct paths from `q` to itself\n * that consume the same word `w`.\n *\n * For any such state `q`, an attack string can be constructed as follows:\n * concatenate a prefix `v` that takes the NFA to `q` with `n` copies of\n * the word `w` that leads back to `q` along two different paths, followed\n * by a suffix `x` that is _not_ accepted in state `q`. A backtracking\n * implementation will need to explore at least 2^n different ways of going\n * from `q` back to itself while trying to match the `n` copies of `w`\n * before finally giving up.\n *\n * Now in order to identify overlapping cycles, all we have to do is find\n * pumpable forks, that is, states `q` that can transition to two different\n * states `r1` and `r2` on the same input symbol `c`, such that there are\n * paths from both `r1` and `r2` to `q` that consume the same word. The latter\n * condition is equivalent to saying that `(q, q)` is reachable from `(r1, r2)`\n * in the product NFA.\n *\n * This is what the library does. It makes a simple attempt to construct a\n * prefix `v` leading into `q`, but only to improve the alert message.\n * And the library tries to prove the existence of a suffix that ensures\n * rejection. This check might fail, which can cause false positives.\n *\n * Finally, sometimes it depends on the translation whether the NFA generated\n * for a regular expression has a pumpable fork or not. We implement one\n * particular translation, which may result in false positives or negatives\n * relative to some particular JavaScript engine.\n *\n * More precisely, the library constructs an NFA from a regular expression `r`\n * as follows:\n *\n *   * Every sub-term `t` gives rise to an NFA state `Match(t,i)`, representing\n *     the state of the automaton before attempting to match the `i`th character in `t`.\n *   * There is one accepting state `Accept(r)`.\n *   * There is a special `AcceptAnySuffix(r)` state, which accepts any suffix string\n *     by using an epsilon transition to `Accept(r)` and an any transition to itself.\n *   * Transitions between states may be labelled with epsilon, or an abstract\n *     input symbol.\n *   * Each abstract input symbol represents a set of concrete input characters:\n *     either a single character, a set of characters represented by a\n *     character class, or the set of all characters.\n *   * The product automaton is constructed lazily, starting with pair states\n *     `(q, q)` where `q` is a fork, and proceeding along an over-approximate\n *     step relation.\n *   * The over-approximate step relation allows transitions along pairs of\n *     abstract input symbols where the symbols have overlap in the characters they accept.\n *   * Once a trace of pairs of abstract input symbols that leads from a fork\n *     back to itself has been identified, we attempt to construct a concrete\n *     string corresponding to it, which may fail.\n *   * Lastly we ensure that any state reached by repeating `n` copies of `w` has\n *     a suffix `x` (possible empty) that is most likely __not__ accepted.\n */\noverlay[local?]\nmodule;\n\nprivate import NfaUtils as NfaUtils\nprivate import stateInsideBacktracking(r2)\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Gets the state pair `(q1, q2)` or `(q2, q1)`; note that only\n   * one or the other is defined.\n   */\n  private StatePair mkStatePair(State q1, State hi = lowercaseLetter()\n      |\n        lo <= char and\n        char <= hi and\n        char = lowercaseLetter()\n      )\n      or\n      exists(string lo, string hi |\n        range.isRange(lo, hi) and lo = upperCaseLetter() and hi = upperCaseLetter()\n      |\n        lo <= char and\n        char <= hi and\n        char = upperCaseLetter()\n      )\n      or\n      exists(string lo, string hi | range.isRange(lo, hi) and lo = digit() and hi = digit() |\n        lo <= char and\n        char <= hi and\n        char = digit()\n      )\n    }\n\n    private string lowercaseLetter() { result = \"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\".charAt(_) }\n\n    private string upperCaseLetter() { result = \"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\".charAt(_) }\n\n    private string digit() { result = [0 .. 9].toString() }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets a char that could be matched by a regular expression.\n     * Includes all printable ascii chars, all constants mentioned in a regexp, and all chars matches by the regexp    classEscapeMatches(_, result)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Gets a char that is mentioned in the character class `c`.\n     */\n    private string getAMentionedChar(RegExpCharacterClass c) {\n child.(RegExpCharacterRange).isRange(_, result)\n        or\n        exists(string charClass | isEscapeClass(child, charClass) |\n          result = min(string s | classEscapeMatches(charClass.toLowerCase(), s))\n          or\n          result = max(string s | classEscapeMatches(charClass.toLowerCase(), s))\n        )\n      )\n    }\n\n    bindingset[char, cc]\n    private string caseNormalize(string char, RegExpTerm cc) {\n      if isIgnoreCase(cc.getRootTerm()) then result = char.toLowerCase() else result = char\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * An implementation of `CharacterClass` for positive (non inverted) character classes.\n     */\n    private class PositiveCharacterClass extends CharacterClass {\n      RegExpCharacterClass cc;\n\n override predicate matches(string char) { hasChildThatMatches(cc, char) }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * An implementation of `CharacterClass` for inverted character classes.\n     */\n    private class InvertedCharacterClass extends CharacterClass {\n      RegExpCharacterClass cc;\n\n      InvertedCharacterClass() { this = getCharClassForCanonicalTerm(cc) and cc.isInverted() }\n\n      override string getARelevantChar() {\n        result = nextChar(caseNormalize(getAMentionedChar(cc), cc)) or\n        nextChar(result) = caseNormalize(getAMentionedChar(cc), cc)\n      }\n\n      bindingset[char]\n      override predicate matches(string char) {\n        not hasChildThatMatches(cc, char) and\n        (\n          // detect unsupported char classes that doesn't match anything (e.g. `\\p{L}` in ruby), and don't report any matches\n          hasChildThatMatches(cc, _)\n          or\n          not exists(cc.getAChild()) // [^] still matches everything\n        )\n      }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Holds if the character class escape `clazz` (\\d, \\s, or \\w) matches `char`.\n     */\n    pragma[noinline]\n    private predicate classEscapeMatches(string clazz, string char) {\n      clazz = \"d\" and\n      char = \"0123456789\".charAt(_)\n      or\n      clazz = \"s\" and\n      char = [\" \", \"\\t\", \"\\r\", \"\\n\", 11.toUnicode(), 12.toUnicode()] // 11.toUnicode() of `CharacterClass` for \\d, \\s, and \\w.\n     */\n    private class PositiveCharacterClassEscape extends CharacterClass {\n      string charClass;\n      RegExpTerm cc;\n\n      PositiveCharacterClassEscape() {\n        isEscapeClass(cc, charClass) and\n        this = getCharClassForCanonicalTerm(cc) and\n        charClass = [\"d\", \"s\", \"w\"]\n      }\n\n      override string getARelevantChar() {\n        charClass = \"d\" and\n        result = [\"0\", \"9\"]\n        or\n        charClass = \"s\" and\n        result = \" \"\n        or\n        charClass = \"w\"        charClass = \"D\" and\n        result = [\"a\", \"Z\", \"!\"]\n        or\n        charClass = \"S\" and\n        result = [\"a\", \"9\", \"!\"]\n        or\n        charClass = \"W\" and\n        result = [\" \", \"!\"]\n      }\n\n      bindingset[char]\n      override predicate matches(string char) {\n        not classEscapeMatches(charClass.toLowerCase(), char) and\n        // detect unsupported char classes (e.g. `\\p{L}` in ruby), and don't report any matches\n        classEscapeMatches(charClass.toLowerCase(), _)\n      }\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a representative for all char classes that match the same chars as `c`. */\n    CharacterClass normalize(CharacterClass c) {\n      exists(string normalization |\n        normalization = getNormalizationString(c) and\n        result =\n          min(CharacterClass cc, string raw |\n            getNormalizationString(cc) = normalization and cc = CharClass(raw)\n          |\n            cc order by raw\n          )\n      )\n    }\n\n    /** Gets a string representing all the chars matched by `c` */\n    private string getNormalizationString(CharacterClass c) {\n      (c instanceof PositiveCharacterClass or c instanceof PositiveCharacterClassEscape) and\n      result = concat(string char | c.matches(char) and char = CharacterClasses::getARelevantChar())\n      or\n      (c instanceof InvertedCharacterClass or c instanceof NegativeCharacterClassEscape) and\n      // the string produced by the concat can not contain repeated chars\n      // so by starting the below with \"nn\" we can guarantee that\n      // it will not overlap with the above case.\n      // and a negative char class can never match the same chars as a positive one, so we don't miss any results from this.\n      result =\n EffectivelyPlus instanceof RegExpTerm {\n    EffectivelyPlus() {\n      this instanceof RegExpPlus\n      or\n      exists(RegExpRange range |\n        range.getLowerBound() = 1 and\n min(getAOverlapBetweenCharacterClasses(c, d))\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Gets a char that is matched by both the character classes `c` and `d`.\n   * And `c` and `d` is not the same character class.\n   */\n and\n    d.matches(result) and\n    not c = d\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Gets a character that is represented by both `c` and `d`.\n   */\n  string intersect(InputSymbol c, InputSymbol d) {\n   not (char = \"\\n\" or char = \"\\r\")\n    or\n    result = Any()\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Holds if `state` is a start state.\n   */\n  predicate isStartState(State state) {\n    state = not always have a result even if there is a ReDoS issue in\n     * the regular expression.\n     */\n    string prefix(State state) {\n      lastStartState(state) and\n      result = \"\"\n      or\n RelevantState() {\n        exists(State s | isCandidate(s) | getRoot(s.getRepr()) = getRoot(this.getRepr()))\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * A module for pruning candidate ReDoS states.\n   * The * No check whether a rejected suffix exists has been made.\n     */\n    private predicate isReDoSCandidate(State state, string pump) {\n      isCandidate(state, pump) and\n      not state = predicates are used to ensure that the all states reached from the fork\n     * by repeating `w` have a rejecting suffix.\n     *\n     * For example, a regexp like `/^(a+)+/` will accept any string as long the prefix is\n     * some number of `\"a\"`s, and it is therefore not possible to construct a rejecting suffix.\n     *\n     * A regexp like `/(a+)+$/` or `/(a+)+b/` trivially has a rejecting suffix,\n     * as the suffix \"X\" will cause both the regular expressions to be rejected.\n     *\n     * The string `w` is repeated any number of times because it needs to be\n     * infinitely repeatable for the attack to work.\n     * For the regular expression `/((ab)+)*abab/` the accepting state is not reachable from the fork\n     * using epsilon transitions. But any attempt at repeating `w` will end in a state that accepts all suffixes.\n     */\n    private module SuffixConstruction {\n      /**\n       * Holds if all states reachable from `fork` by repeating `w`\n       * are likely rejectable by appending some suffix.\n       */\n      predicate reachesOnlyRejectableSuffixes(State fork, string w) {\n        isReDoSCandidate(fork, w) and\n        forex(State next | next = process(fork, w, getCodepointLengthForCandidate(w) - 1) |\n          isLikelyRejectable(next)\n        ) and\n        not getProcessPrevious(fork, _, w) = acceptsAnySuffix() // we stop `process(..)` early if we can, check here if it happened.\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if there likely exists a suffix starting from `s` that leads to the regular expression being rejected.\n       * This predicate might find impossible suffixes when searching for suffixes of length > 1, which can cause FPs.\n       */\n      pragma[noinline]\n      private predicate isLikelyRejectable(RelevantState s) {\n        // exists a reject edge with some char.\n        hasRejectEdge(s)\n        or\n        hasEdgeToLikelyRejectable(s)\n        or\n        // stopping here is rejection\n        isRejectState(s)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if `s` is not an accept state, and there is no epsilon transition to an accept state.\n       */\n      predicate isRejectState(RelevantState s) { not epsilonSucc*(s) = Accept(_) }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if there is likely a non-empty suffix leading to rejection starting in `s`.\n       */\n      pragma[noopt]\n      predicate hasEdgeToLikelyRejectable(RelevantState s) {\n        // all edges (at least one) with some char leads to another state that is rejectable.\n        // the `next` states might not share a common suffix, which can cause FPs.\n        exists(string char | char = hasEdgeToLikelyRejectableHelper(s) |\n          // noopt to force `hasEdgeToLikelyRejectableHelper` to be first in the join-order.\n          exists(State next | deltaClosedChar(s, char, next) | isLikelyRejectable(next)) and\n          forall(State next | deltaClosedChar(s, char, next) | isLikelyRejectable(next))\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Gets a char for there exists a transition away from `s`,\n       * and `s` has not been found to be rejectable by `hasRejectEdge` or `isRejectState`.\n       */\n      pragma[noinline]\n      private string hasEdgeToLikelyRejectableHelper(RelevantState s) {\n        not hasRejectEdge(s) and\n        not isRejectState(s) and\n        deltaClosedChar(s, result, _)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if there is a state `next` that can be reached from `prev`\n       * along epsilon edges, such that there is a transition from\n       * `prev` to `next` that the character symbol `char`.\n       */\n      predicate deltaClosedChar(RelevantState prev, string char, RelevantState next) {\n        deltaClosed(prev, | result = intersect(s, _))\n          or\n          // The characters from `hasSimpleRejectEdge`. The three chars must be kept in sync with `relevant`.\n        exists(string char | char = [\"|\", \"\\n\", \"Z\"] | not deltaClosedChar(s, char, _))\n      }\n\n      // `process` can't use pragma[inline] predicates. So a materialized version of `getCodepointAt` is needed.\n      pragma[noinline]\n      private string getCodePointAtForProcess(string str, int i) {\n        result = getCodepointAt(str, i) and\n        isReDoSCandidate(_, str)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Gets a state that can be reached from pumpable `fork` consuming all\n       * chars in `w` any number of times followed by the first `i+1` characters of `w`.\n       */\n      pragma[noopt]\n      private State process(State fork, string w, int i) {\n        exists(State prev | prev = getProcessPrevious(fork, i, w) |\n          not prev = acceptsAnySuffix() and // we stop `process(..)` early if we can. If the successor accepts any suffix, then we know it can never be rejected.\n          exists(string char, InputSymbol sym |\n            char = getCodePointAtForProcess(w, i) and\n            deltaClosed(prev, sym, result) and\n            // noopt to prevent joining `prev` with all possible `chars` that could transition away from `prev`.\n            // Instead only join with the set of `fork` consuming all\n       * chars in `w` any number of times followed by the first `i` characters of `w`.\n       */\n      private State getProcessPrevious(State fork, int i, string w) {\n        isReDoSCandidate(fork, w) and\n        (\n          i = 0 and result = fork\n          or\n          result = process(fork, w, i - 1)\n          or\n          // repeat until fixpoint\n          i = 0 and\n          result = process(fork, w, getCodepointLengthForCandidate(w) - 1)\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Gets an InputSymbol that matches `char`.\n       * The predicate is getAProcessChar() and\n        result = getAnInputSymbolMatching(char)\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Gets a `char` that occurs in a `pump` string.\n       */\n      private string getAProcessChar() (see `getAThreewayIntersect`)\n *\n * We start a search in the product automaton at `(pivot, pivot, pumpEnd)`,\n * and search for a series of transitions (a `Trace`), such that we end\n * at `(pivot, pumpEnd, pumpEnd)` (see `isReachableFromStartTuple`).\n *\n * For example, consider the regular expression `/^\\d*5\\w*$/`.\n * The search will start at the tuple `(\\d*, \\d*, \\w*)` and search\n * for a path to `(\\d*, \\w*, \\w*)`.\n * This path exists, and consists of a single transition in the product automaton,\n * where the three corresponding NFA edges all match the character `\"5\"`.\n *\n * The start-state in the NFA has an any-transition to itself, this allows us to\n * flag regular expressions such as `/a*$/` - pragma[noopt]\n  predicate step(\n    StateTuple q, InputSymbol s1, InputSymbol s2, InputSymbol s3, State r1, State r2, State r3\n  ) {\n    exists(State q1, State q2, State q3 | q.isTuple(q1, q2, q3) exists(getAThreewayIntersect(s1, s2, s3))\n    )\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Gets a char that is matched by all the edges `s1`, `s2`, and `s3`.\n   *\n   * The result is not complete, and might miss some /**\n   * Holds if `bb` is in the dominance frontier of a block containing a\n   * read of `v`.\n   */\n  pragma[nomagic]\n  private predicate inReadDominanceFrontier(BasicBlock bb, SourceVariable v) node.\n   *\n   * Phi-read nodes are like normal phi nodes, but they are inserted based on reads\n   * instead of writes, and only if the dominance-frontier block does not already\n   * contain a normal phi node.\n   *\n   * The motivation for adding phi-reads is to improve performance of the use-use\n   * calculation in cases where there is a large number of reads that can reach the\n   * same join-point, and from there reach a large number of basic blocks. Example:\n   *\n   * ```cs\n   * if (a)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (b)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (c)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (d)\n   *   use(x);\n   * // many more ifs ...\n   *\n   * // phi-read for `x` inserted here\n   *\n   * // program not mentioning `x`, with large basic block graph\n   *\n   * use(x);\n   * ```\n   *\n   * Without phi-reads, the analysis has to replicate reachability for each of\n   * the guarded uses of `x`. However, with phi-reads, the analysis will limit\n   * each conditional use of `x` to reach the basic block containing the phi-read\n   * node for `x`, and only that basic block will have to compute reachability\n   * through the remainder of the large program.\n   *\n   * Another motivation for phi-reads is when a large number of reads can reach\n   * another large number of reads:\n   *\n   * ```cs\n   * if (a)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (b)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (c)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (d)\n   *   use(x);\n   * // many more ifs ...\n   *\n   * // phi-read for `x` inserted here\n   *\n   * if (a)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (b)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (c)\n   *   use(x);\n   * else if (d)\n   *   use(x);\n   * // many more ifs ...\n   * ```\n   *\n   * Without phi-reads, one needs to add `n*m` data-flow edges (assuming `n` reads\n   * before the phi-read and `m` reads after the phi-read), whereas if we include\n   * phi-reads in the data-flow graph, we only need to add `n+m` edges.\n   *\n   * Like normal reads, each phi-read node `phi-read` can be reached from exactly\n   * one SSA definition (without passing through another definition): Assume, for\n   * the sake of contradiction, that there are two reaching definitions `def1` and\n   * `def2`. Now, if both `def1` and `def2` dominate `phi-read`, then the nearest\n   * dominating definition will prevent the other from reaching `phi-read`. So, at\n   * least one of `def1` and `def2` cannot dominate `phi-read`; assume it is `def1`.\n   * Then `def1` must go through one of its dominance-frontier blocks in order to\n   * reach `phi-read`. However, such a block will always start with a (normal) phi\n   * node, which contradicts reachability.\n   *\n   * Also, like normal reads, the unique SSA definition `def` that reaches `phi-read`,\n   * will dominate `phi-read`. 1) and\n            path = getNthTypeParameterPath(constraint, tp, i)\n          )\n        )\n      }\n\n      private predicate typeParametersEqual(\n        App app, TypeAbstraction abs, Constraint constraint, TypeParameter tp\n      ) {\n        satisfiesConcreteTypes(app, abs, constraint) and\n        tp = getNthTypeParameter(abs, _) and\n        (\n          not exists(getNthTypeParameterPath(constraint, tp, _))\n          or\n          exists(int n | n = max(int i | exists(getNthTypeParameterPath(constraint, tp, i))) |\n            // If the largest index is 0, then there are no equalities to check as\n            // the type parameter only occurs once.\n            if n = 0 then any() else typeParametersEqualFromIndex(app, abs, constraint, tp, _, n)\n          )\n        )\n      }\n\n      private predicate typeParametersHaveEqualInstantiationFromIndex(\n        App app, TypeAbstraction abs, Constraint constraint, int i\n      ) {\n        exists(TypeParameter tp | tp = getNthTypeParameter(abs, i) |\n          typeParametersEqual(app, abs, constraint, tp) and\n          if i = 0\n          then any()\n          else typeParametersHaveEqualInstantiationFromIndex(app, abs, constraint, i - 1)\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if `app` is a possible instantiation of `constraint`. That is, by making\n       * appropriate substitutions for the free type parameters in `constraint` given by\n       * `abs`, it is possible to obtain `app`.\n       *\n       * For instance, if `A` and `B` are free type parameters we have:\n       * - `Pair<int, string>` is an instantiation of       `A`\n       * - `Pair<int, string>` is an instantiation of       `Pair<A, B>`\n       * - `Pair<int, int>`    is an instantiation of       `Pair<A, A>`\n       * - `Pair<int, bool>`   is _not_ an instantiation of `Pair<A, A>`\n       * - `Pair<int, string>` is _not_ an instantiation of `Pair<string, string>`\n       */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isInstantiationOf(App app, TypeAbstraction abs, Constraint constraint) {\n        // We only need to check equality if the concrete types are satisfied.\n        satisfiesConcreteTypes(app, abs, constraint) and\n        // Check if all the places where the same type parameter occurs in `constraint`\n        // are equal in `app`.\n        //\n        // TODO: As of now this only checks equality at the root of the types\n        // instantiated for type parameters. So, for instance, `Pair<Vec<i64>, Vec<bool>>`\n        // is mistakenly considered an instantiation of `Pair<A, A>`.\n        (\n          not exists(getNthTypeParameter(abs, _))\n          or\n          exists(int n | n = max(int i | exists(getNthTypeParameter(abs, i))) |\n            typeParametersHaveEqualInstantiationFromIndex(app, abs, constraint, n)\n          )\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if `app` is _not_ a possible instantiation of `constraint`.\n       *\n       * This is an approximation of `not isInstantiationOf(app, abs, constraint)`, but\n       * defined without a negative occurrence of `isInstantiationOf`.\n       *\n       * Due to the approximation, both `isInstantiationOf` and `isNotInstantiationOf`\n       * can hold for the same values. For example, if `app` has two different types `t1`\n       * and `t2` at the same type path, and `t1` satisfies `constraint` while `t2` does\n       * not, then both `isInstantiationOf` and `isNotInstantiationOf` will hold.\n       *\n       * Dually, if `app` does not have a type at a required type path, then neither\n       * `isInstantiationOf` nor `isNotInstantiationOf` will hold.\n       */\n      pragma[nomagic]\n      predicate isNotInstantiationOf(App app, TypeAbstraction abs, Constraint constraint) {\n        // `app` and `constraint` differ on a concrete type\n        exists(Type t, Type t2, TypePath path |\n          t = resolveTypeAt(app, abs, constraint, path) and\n          not t = abs.getATypeParameter() and\n          app.getTypeAt(path) = t2 and\n          t2 != t\n        )\n      }\n    }\n\n    /** Provides logic related to base types. */\n    module BaseTypes {\n      /**\n       * Holds if, when `tm1` is considered an instantiation of `tm2`, then at\n       * the type parameter `tp` it has the type `t` at `path`.\n       *\n       * For instance, if the type `Map<int, List<int>>` is considered an\n       * instantion of `Map<K, V>` then it has the type `int` at `K` and the\n       * type `List<int>` at `V`.\n       */\n      bindingset[tm1, tm2]\n      private predicate instantiatesWith(\n        TypeMention tm1, TypeMention tm2, TypeParameter tp, TypePath path, Type t\n      ) {\n        exists(TypePath prefix |\n          tm2.resolveTypeAt(prefix) = tp and t = tm1.resolveTypeAt(prefix.appendInverse(path))\n        )\n      }\n\n      private module IsInstantiationOfInput implements\n        IsInstantiationOfInputSig<TypeMentionTypeTree, TypeMentionTypeTree>\n      {\n        pragma[nomagic]\n        private predicate typeCondition(\n          Type type, TypeAbstraction abs, TypeMentionTypeTree condition\n        ) {\n          conditionSatisfiesConstraint(abs, condition, _) and\n          type = resolveTypeMentionRoot(condition)\n        }\n\n        pragma[nomagic]\n        private predicate typeConstraint(Type type, TypeMentionTypeTree constraint) {\n          conditionSatisfiesConstraint(_, _, constraint) and\n          type = resolveTypeMentionRoot(constraint)\n        }\n\n        predicate potentialInstantiationOf(\n          TypeMentionTypeTree constraint, TypeAbstraction abs, TypeMentionTypeTree condition\n        ) {\n          exists(Type type |\n            typeConstraint(type, constraint) and typeCondition(type, abs, condition)\n          )\n        }\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if the type mention `condition` satisfies `constraint` with the\n       * type `t` at the path `path`.\n       */\n      predicate conditionSatisfiesConstraintTypeAt(\n        TypeAbstraction abs, TypeMention condition, TypeMention constraint, TypePath path, Type t\n      ) {\n        // base case\n        conditionSatisfiesConstraint(abs, condition, constraint) and\n        constraint.resolveTypeAt(path) = t\n        or\n        // recursive case\n        exists(TypeAbstraction midAbs, TypeMention midConstraint, TypeMention midCondition |\n          conditionSatisfiesConstraint(abs, condition, midConstraint) and\n          // NOTE: `midAbs` describe the free type variables in `midCondition`, midAbs, midCondition)\n        |\n          conditionSatisfiesConstraintTypeAt(midAbs, midCondition, constraint, path, t) and\n          not t = midAbs.getATypeParameter()\n          or\n tp) and\n            instantiatesWith(midConstraint, midCondition, tp, suffix, t) and\n            path = prefix.append(suffix)\n          )\n        )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if it's conditionSatisfiesConstraintTypeAt(abs, condition, constraint, _, _) and\n        conditionRoot = resolveTypeMentionRoot(condition) and\n        constraintRoot = resolveTypeMentionRoot(constraint)\n       */\n      int countConstraintImplementations(Type conditionRoot, Type constraintRoot) {\n        result =\n          strictcount(TypeAbstraction abs, TypeMention tm, TypeMention constraint |\n            rootTypesSatisfaction(conditionRoot, constraintRoot, abs, tm, constraint)\n          |\n            constraint\n          )\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if there is multiple ways in which a type with `conditionRoot` at\n       * the root can satisfy a constraint with `constraintRoot` at the root.\n       */\n      predicate multipleConstraintImplementations(Type conditionRoot, Type constraintRoot) {\n        countConstraintImplementations(conditionRoot, constraintRoot) > 1\n      }\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if `baseMention` is a (transitive) base type mention of `sub`,\n       * and `t` is mentioned (implicitly) at `path` inside `baseMention`. pragma[only_bind_into](immediateBaseMention) =\n            getABaseTypeMention(pragma[only_bind_into](sub))\n        |\n          // immediate base class\n          baseMention = immediateBaseMention resolveTypeMentionRoot(immediateBaseMention) |\n            baseTypeMentionHasNonTypeParameterAt(immediateBase, baseMention, path, t)\n            or\n            exists(TypePath path0, TypePath prefix, TypePath suffix, TypeParameter tp |\n              /*\n               * Example:\n               *\n               * - `prefix = \"T2.T1\"`,\n               * - `path0 = \"T3\"`,\n      * class Base<T2> { }\n               *\n               * class Mid<T3> : Base<C<T3>> { }\n               * //    ^^^ `immediateBase`\n               * //        ^^ `tp`\n               * // overlay[caller?]\n      pragma[inline]\n      predicate baseTypeMentionHasNonTypeParameterAt(\n        Type sub, TypeMention baseMention, TypePath path, Type t\n      ) {\n        not t = sub.getATypeParameter() and baseTypeMentionHasTypeAt(sub, baseMention, path, t)\n      }\n\n      overlay[caller?]\n      pragma[inline]\n      predicate baseTypeMentionHasTypeParameterAt(\n        Type sub, TypeMention baseMention, TypePath path, TypeParameter tp\n      ) {\n        tp = sub.getATypeParameter() and baseTypeMentionHasTypeAt(sub, baseMention, path, tp)\n      }\n    }\n\n    private import BaseTypes\n\n    signature module SatisfiesConstraintInputSig<HasTypeTreeSig HasTypeTree> {\n      /** Holds if it is relevant to know if `term` satisfies `constraint`. */\n      predicate relevantConstraint(HasTypeTree term, Type constraint);\n\n      /**\n       * Holds if constraints that are satisfied through conditions that are\n       * universally quantified type Hence using these represent a trade-off between too many\n       * constraints and too few constraints being satisfied.\n       */\n      default predicate useUniversalConditions() { any() }\n satisfiesConstraintTypeMention0(\n        HasTypeTree tt, Type constraint, TypeAbstraction abs, TypeMention sub, TypePath path, Type t\n      ) {\n        exists(TypeMention constraintMention |\n pragma[nomagic]\n      private predicate satisfiesConstraintTypeMention1(\n        HasTypeTree tt, Type constraint, TypePath path, TypePath pathToTypeParamInSub\n      ) {\n because `step/3` becomes a recursive call, which means\n   * that we will have a conjunct with 3 recursive calls: the call to `step`, the call to\n   * `stepProj`, and the recursive type tracking call
